Banyan.description: The national tree of India, famous for its massive canopy and extensive aerial prop roots that anchor into the ground to form secondary trunks.
Banyan.habitat: Widespread across the Indo-Gangetic plains, Deccan Plateau, roadside avenues, village squares, and sacred temple groves throughout India.
Banyan.active_compounds: Bengalenoside, Flavonoids, Tannins, Ficusin, Beta-sitosterol, Lupeol
Banyan.watering: Moderate; deep taproots and aerial prop roots make mature trees exceptionally drought-hardy
Banyan.soil: Deep, well-draining alluvial, sandy loam, or rocky soil; highly adaptable
Banyan.toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic to dogs and cats; milky latex sap can cause oral irritation and vomiting
Banyan.uses: Extensive shade canopy, soil conservation, avenue planting, traditional timber for carts, and spiritual veneration.
Banyan.ayurvedic_uses: Bark astringent used in Kashaya for diabetes (Prameha), dysentery, diarrhea, and toothache; milky sap applied topically to ulcers and cracked soles.

Sacred Fig (Peepal).description: A sacred deciduous tree revered across India, easily recognized by its heart-shaped leaves with an elongated slender drip tip that rustles in the gentlest breeze.
Sacred Fig (Peepal).habitat: Found throughout the Indian subcontinent from the Sub-Himalayan foothills to southern peninsular India; common in temple complexes and urban areas.
Sacred Fig (Peepal).active_compounds: Kaempferol, Quercetin, Myricetin, Stigmasterol, Tannins, Vitamin K
Sacred Fig (Peepal).watering: Low to Moderate; highly tolerant of seasonal dry spells
Sacred Fig (Peepal).soil: Extremely hardy; thrives in rocky fissures, calcareous soils, and brick masonry
Sacred Fig (Peepal).toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic to pets; sap can cause gastrointestinal distress and dermatitis
Sacred Fig (Peepal).uses: Spiritual significance, oxygen production, urban greenery, sacred groves, and traditional paper crafting.
Sacred Fig (Peepal).ayurvedic_uses: Bark decoction used for asthma, diabetes, wound healing, and skin diseases; tender leaves and figs used as blood purifiers and for gynecological disorders.

Neem Tree.description: A fast-growing evergreen tree known as 'Nature's Pharmacy', celebrated for its dense shade and bitter, pest-repelling leaves.
Neem Tree.habitat: Thrives in dry, arid, and semi-arid regions of central, western, and southern India, including Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra.
Neem Tree.active_compounds: Azadirachtin, Nimbin, Nimbidin, Gedunin, Salannin, Quercetin
Neem Tree.watering: Low; drought-tolerant once established and thrives in hot climates
Neem Tree.soil: Well-drained sandy, stony, or clayey soils; tolerates acidic to highly alkaline soils (pH 6.2 - 8.5)
Neem Tree.toxicity_pets: Foliage non-toxic in small amounts; concentrated neem oil and seeds can cause gastrointestinal toxicity in pets
Neem Tree.uses: Bio-pesticide production, herbal cosmetics, organic fertilizers, mosquito repellent, and traditional toothbrushes (datun).
Neem Tree.ayurvedic_uses: Premier cooling blood purifier (Tikta Rasa); pacifies Pitta and Kapha; used for acne, eczema, psoriasis, fever, intestinal worms, and diabetes.

Mango Tree.description: A magnificent large tropical evergreen tree with a broad rounded canopy, yielding the National Fruit of India during the warm summer season.
Mango Tree.habitat: Native to tropical South Asia, cultivated extensively across Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and West Bengal.
Mango Tree.active_compounds: Mangiferin, Quercetin, Kaempferol, Gallic acid, Beta-carotene, Lupeol
Mango Tree.watering: Moderate; requires regular watering during fruit setting and dry weather before flowering
Mango Tree.soil: Deep, fertile, well-draining loamy or alluvial soil with pH 5.5 - 7.5
Mango Tree.toxicity_pets: Flesh non-toxic; tree bark, leaves, and fruit peel contain urushiol-related allergens that may cause mild allergic dermatitis in pets
Mango Tree.uses: Fruit timber, shade canopy, ornamental tree, and leaves used extensively in Hindu auspicious ceremonies (Toran).
Mango Tree.ayurvedic_uses: Leaves and bark decoction used in bleeding dysentery, gingivitis, and blood sugar control; seed kernel used for astringent bowel disorders.

Coconut Palm.description: A graceful unbranched palm tree rising up to 30 meters, hailed as the 'tree of life' or Kalpavriksha because every single part is utilized.
Coconut Palm.habitat: Lush coastal belts of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Maharashtra, Odisha, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
Coconut Palm.active_compounds: Lauric acid, Cytokinins, Monolaurin, Polyphenols, Potassium, Electrolytes
Coconut Palm.watering: High; requires high atmospheric humidity and abundant groundwater
Coconut Palm.soil: Sandy loam, alluvial coastal sands, or lateritic soils with good drainage
Coconut Palm.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; coconut water and meat are safe in moderation; husk represents a physical bowel obstruction hazard
Coconut Palm.uses: Coir fiber, copra oil, tender coconut water, leaf thatching, shell handicrafts, and construction timber.
Coconut Palm.ayurvedic_uses: Coconut water (Narikela Udaka) is deeply hydrating, Pitta-pacifying, and cooling; virgin coconut oil nourishes hair, scalp, and skin wounds.

Teak.description: A premier hardwood timber tree with large papery ovate leaves and fragrant small white flowers that produce weather-resistant luxury wood.
Teak.habitat: Central and southern tropical moist and dry deciduous forests in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Kerala (Nilambur), and Gujarat.
Teak.active_compounds: Tectoqunone, Lapachol, Betulinic acid, Tannins, Tectograndin
Teak.watering: Moderate; well adapted to distinct monsoonal wet and dry cycles
Teak.soil: Deep, moist, well-drained alluvial and loamy soils rich in calcium and magnesium
Teak.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets under normal exposure; saw dust may cause mechanical eye and respiratory irritation
Teak.uses: Shipbuilding, high-end furniture, architectural carvings, heavy structural timber, and railway ties.
Teak.ayurvedic_uses: Bark and wood astringent; used to control bleeding, alleviate burning sensation, combat biliousness, and heal skin inflammation.

Sal.description: A magnificent tall deciduous forest tree that dominates eastern and central Indian forests, revered in tribal cultures and religious traditions.
Sal.habitat: Foot of the Himalayas, Terai belt, and the Chota Nagpur plateau covering Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Madhya Pradesh.
Sal.active_compounds: Shobic acid, Shoreaphenol, Ursolic acid, Dammar resin, Tannins
Sal.watering: Moderate; thrives in monsoonal sub-humid subtropical conditions
Sal.soil: Deep, fertile sandy loam to red lateritic soils with good moisture retention
Sal.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; resin is inert
Sal.uses: Heavy construction timber, railway sleepers, Sal resin (Dammar) used as incense and sealant, leaves for biodegradable dining plates (patravali).
Sal.ayurvedic_uses: Resin (Ral) used as an astringent and antimicrobial for skin ulcers, dysentery, burn wounds, and ear infections.

Ashoka.description: A sacred rainforest tree famous for its heavy bunches of fragrant orange-red flowers that emerge directly from mature branches.
Ashoka.habitat: Rainforests of the Western Ghats, Eastern Himalayas, and wet tropical zones; often planted near sacred temples.
Ashoka.active_compounds: Saracin, Catechin, Epicatechin, Leucocyanidin, Tannins, Phytoestrogens
Ashoka.watering: Moderate to High; prefers moist, humus-rich soil conditions
Ashoka.soil: Fertile, moist, well-draining red loamy or laterite soils
Ashoka.uses: Sacred groves, ornamental planting, landscape horticulture, and classical Ayurvedic formulation manufacturing.
Ashoka.ayurvedic_uses: Renowned female reproductive tonic (Ashokarishta); effective against menorrhagia, dysmenorrhea, uterine fibroids, and internal hemorrhoids.

Gulmohar (Royal Poinciana).description: A broad, umbrella-shaped avenue tree famed for its sensational explosion of fiery scarlet and orange blossoms during April and June.
Gulmohar (Royal Poinciana).habitat: Grown along avenues, parks, and institutional campuses across almost all plains and coastal zones of India.
Gulmohar (Royal Poinciana).watering: Low to Moderate; highly drought-hardy once fully grown
Gulmohar (Royal Poinciana).soil: Tolerates poor, sandy, loamy, and urban clay soils as long as drainage is adequate
Gulmohar (Royal Poinciana).toxicity_pets: Pods and seeds may cause digestive upset if consumed in large quantities by pets
Gulmohar (Royal Poinciana).uses: Spectacular ornamental avenue shade tree, urban landscape architecture, and flowering park centerpiece.
Gulmohar (Royal Poinciana).ayurvedic_uses: Flowers and bark used folk-medicinally for rheumatism, constipation, pyrexia, and inflammatory joint swelling.

Jamun (Java Plum).description: A majestic evergreen tropical tree producing dense clusters of dark purple astringent-sweet berries that turn the tongue purple.
Jamun (Java Plum).habitat: Abundant along riverbanks, moist deciduous forests, and cultivated orchards across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Punjab.
Jamun (Java Plum).active_compounds: Jamboline, Jambosine, Ellagic acid, Anthocyanins, Gallic acid, Ferulic acid
Jamun (Java Plum).watering: Moderate; tolerates seasonal flooding and waterlogged conditions well
Jamun (Java Plum).soil: Deep, moisture-retentive loamy, alluvial, or clay soils
Jamun (Java Plum).toxicity_pets: Fruit flesh is safe; large pits represent a potential choking hazard and mild cyanogenic risk in bulk
Jamun (Java Plum).uses: Edible summer fruit, timber for agricultural implements and water wheels, vinegar preparation, and nectar for honeybees.
Jamun (Java Plum).ayurvedic_uses: Seeds (Jambu Beeja) are widely prescribed in Ayurveda for Madhumeha (Type-2 Diabetes) to control blood glucose and glucosuria.

Amla (Indian Gooseberry).description: A small-to-medium deciduous tree with feathery branchlets and translucent yellowish-green spherical fruits famous for immense Vitamin C content.
Amla (Indian Gooseberry).habitat: Deciduous forests of peninsular India, foothills of the Himalayas, and widely cultivated in Uttar Pradesh (Pratapgarh), Madhya Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
Amla (Indian Gooseberry).active_compounds: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C), Emblicanin A & B, Ellagic acid, Gallic acid, Chebulagic acid
Amla (Indian Gooseberry).watering: Moderate; drought-resistant once root system develops
Amla (Indian Gooseberry).soil: Light loamy, alluvial, or moderately sodic and calcareous soils (pH 6.5 - 8.5)
Amla (Indian Gooseberry).toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe antioxidant fruit
Amla (Indian Gooseberry).uses: Culinary pickles, candies, Triphala rasayana production, hair conditioners, inks, and dyes.
Amla (Indian Gooseberry).ayurvedic_uses: Revered as Rasayana (longevity tonic) in Chyawanprash; balances all three Doshas (Vata, Pitta, Kapha); boosts immunity, vision, and digestive agni.

Tamarind.description: A massive, long-lived evergreen tree with dense drooping foliage and brown pod-like fruits filled with sour, tart, sticky pulp.
Tamarind.habitat: Ubiquitous along highways, open dry plains, rural farmland borders, and temple towns of South and Central India.
Tamarind.active_compounds: Tartaric acid, Citric acid, Pectin, Lupeol, Catechin, Epicatechin
Tamarind.watering: Low to Moderate; highly drought-resistant and wind-firm
Tamarind.soil: Deep, alluvial, porous loamy or gravelly soils; tolerates saline coastal soils
Tamarind.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; tart pulp may cause mild laxative effects if eaten in excess
Tamarind.uses: Essential culinary souring agent in sambar, rasam, and chutneys; hard durable timber for pestles, charcoal, and avenue shade.
Tamarind.ayurvedic_uses: Ripe fruit stimulates digestion and acts as a mild laxative; seed powder applied for joint sprains; leaves used in hot poultices for swellings.

Jackfruit Tree.description: A stately tropical evergreen tree yielding the largest tree-borne fruit in the botanical world, bearing massive prickly green fruits directly on its trunk.
Jackfruit Tree.habitat: Indigenous to the rainforests of the Western Ghats; grown abundantly throughout Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Assam.
Jackfruit Tree.active_compounds: Artocarpin, Artocarpetin, Moric acid, Jacalin, Carotenoids, Dietary fiber
Jackfruit Tree.watering: Moderate; requires adequate moisture during youth and fruit formation
Jackfruit Tree.soil: Deep, fertile, well-draining alluvial or red lateritic loam
Jackfruit Tree.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; seeds should be cooked or removed to prevent choking
Jackfruit Tree.uses: Unripe fruit used as vegetable meat substitute, ripe fruit eaten fresh, durable golden timber used for musical instruments (veena, mridangam).
Jackfruit Tree.ayurvedic_uses: Root extract used for fever and skin disease; roasted seeds nourish Shukra Dhatu; unripe fruit pacifies Vata while building body mass.

Arjuna.description: A majestic buttressed tree with smooth, grey, peeling bark and five-winged fruit pods, traditionally lining Indian river courses and streams.
Arjuna.habitat: Riverbanks, ravines, and dry stream valleys across Central, Eastern, and Southern India, especially Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, and Maharashtra.
Arjuna.active_compounds: Arjunic acid, Arjunolic acid, Arjunetin, Arjungenin, Tannins, Coenzyme Q10 analogs
Arjuna.watering: Moderate to High; prefers moist sub-surface water availability
Arjuna.soil: Fertile alluvial, loamy, and riverine soils with high moisture content
Arjuna.uses: Riverbank soil stabilization, avenue shading, silk moth host (Tasar silk cultivation), and wood for agricultural carts.
Arjuna.ayurvedic_uses: Renowned cardio-protective tonic (Hridya); strengthens heart muscle, reduces angina, regulates blood pressure, and heals bone fractures.

Sandalwood.description: A prized, slow-growing hemi-parasitic small tree famed worldwide for its aromatic, golden-yellow, essential-oil-rich heartwood.
Sandalwood.habitat: Dry deciduous forests of southern India, especially Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and parts of Andhra Pradesh and Kerala.
Sandalwood.watering: Low to Moderate; susceptible to waterlogging
Sandalwood.soil: Red ferruginous, gravelly, or sandy loam soils with rapid drainage
Sandalwood.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe aromatic wood
Sandalwood.uses: High-value sandalwood oil perfumery, religious tilak paste, luxury soaps, handicrafts, and spiritual rituals.
Sandalwood.ayurvedic_uses: Exquisite cooling Pitta-pacifying herb; applied to forehead for burning fevers and migraines; treats acne, sunburn, and urinary tract burning.

regional_names.tamil: சிசு மரம் (Sisu maram) / ஈட்டி மரம் (Eetti maram)

Indian Rosewood (Sheesham).description: A premier timber tree of North India with light green pinnate foliage and rugged grey bark that yields rich brown, durable, golden-grained timber.
Indian Rosewood (Sheesham).habitat: Sub-Himalayan valleys, riverbeds, and cultivated farm borders across Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar.
Indian Rosewood (Sheesham).watering: Moderate; drought-resistant with deep taproot system
Indian Rosewood (Sheesham).soil: Porous sandy, alluvial, and gravelly soils; nitrogen-fixing roots enrich soil fertility
Indian Rosewood (Sheesham).uses: High-grade luxury furniture, export cabinetry, wood carvings, musical instruments, and shade along canal banks.
Indian Rosewood (Sheesham).ayurvedic_uses: Wood and bark decoction used as blood purifier for leprosy, skin eruptions, sciatica, and chronic ulcers; leaves alleviate burning micturition.

Bamboo.description: A giant arborescent woody clumping grass forming dense thorny thickets with soaring hollow culms that grow at astonishing daily rates.
Bamboo.habitat: Moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests across the Western Ghats, Assam, Meghalaya, and central Indian river valleys.
Bamboo.active_compounds: Silica, Choline, Betaine, Bambusaponin, Tabasheer (Vanshlochan), Flavonoids
Bamboo.watering: Moderate to High; thrives along moist forest valleys
Bamboo.soil: Fertile, moist alluvial or sandy loams with good drainage
Bamboo.toxicity_pets: Culms non-toxic; raw young shoots contain cyanogenic taxiphyllin that requires boiling before consumption
Bamboo.uses: Scaffolding, eco-friendly rural construction, paper pulp, woven handicrafts, fencing, and edible shoots.
Bamboo.ayurvedic_uses: Siliceous secretion (Vanshlochan / Tabasheer) is an excellent tonic for cough, asthma, debility, burning sensation, and tuberculosis.

regional_names.tamil: நீலகிரி மரம் (Neelagiri maram) / தைல மரம் (Thaila maram)

Eucalyptus.description: A soaring aromatic evergreen tree with peeling bluish-grey bark, slender sickle-shaped leaves, and strong cineole-scented essential oils.
Eucalyptus.habitat: Introduced in the mid-19th century; widely naturalized in the Nilgiri Hills, Western Ghats, and farmed across Punjab, Haryana, and Karnataka.
Eucalyptus.watering: Low to Moderate; deep roots rapidly absorb subsoil moisture
Eucalyptus.soil: Tolerates poor, acidic, well-draining soils; avoids heavy stagnant clay
Eucalyptus.toxicity_pets: Toxic to dogs and cats; concentrated eucalyptus oil causes salivation, vomiting, diarrhea, and lethargy
Eucalyptus.uses: Paper and rayon pulp, timber poles, essential eucalyptus oil distillation for respiratory balms, and windbreaks.
Eucalyptus.ayurvedic_uses: Tailaparna oil inhaled for sinusitis, rhinitis, chest congestion, asthma, and applied topically as a warming analgesic for arthritic pain.

regional_names.tamil: ஆயில் மரம் (Aayil maram) / அவல் மரம் (Aval maram)

Indian Elm.description: A large spreading deciduous tree bearing distinctive flat, winged samara seeds that flutter down in dense carpets before monsoons.
Indian Elm.habitat: Dry and moist deciduous forests of central and northern India, common across Rajasthan, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Deccan dry areas.
Indian Elm.active_compounds: Holoptelin A & B, Beta-sitosterol, Friedelin, Betulinic acid, Hexacosanol
Indian Elm.watering: Low; drought-tolerant and resilient to high ambient heat
Indian Elm.soil: Grows vigorously in sandy loam, gravelly, and rocky soils; resists urban roadside pollution
Indian Elm.uses: Avenue shade tree, wood for light carpentry and packing cases, urban pollution mitigation, and cattle fodder.
Indian Elm.ayurvedic_uses: Bark paste used for scabies, eczema, rheumatism, and ringworm; Chirabilva balances Kapha and Pitta; used in hemorrhoids and piles.

Kadamba.description: A magnificent broad-leaved tropical tree associated with Lord Krishna, famous for its sweet-scented golden globe-like inflorescences.
Kadamba.habitat: Moist deciduous and evergreen forests of Assam, Bengal, Odisha, Karnataka, and Western Ghat valleys.
Kadamba.active_compounds: Cadambine, Cadamine, Cinchotannic acid, Ursolic acid, Saponins
Kadamba.watering: Moderate to High; thrives near freshwater sources and rainy tracts
Kadamba.soil: Deep, moist, well-aerated alluvial or sandy loam soils
Kadamba.uses: Sacred ornamental temple planting, shade avenues, matchwood, paper pulp, and essential oil perfume extraction.
Kadamba.ayurvedic_uses: Bark and fruit decoctions used to treat stomatitis, diabetic wounds, venomous bites, intestinal worms, and uterine bleeding.

Palash (Flame of the Forest).species: Palash Tree (Flame of the Forest / Bastard Teak)
Palash (Flame of the Forest).description: A medium-sized deciduous tree whose canopy turns into a sea of blazing vermilion-orange flowers in spring, heralding the festival of Holi.
Palash (Flame of the Forest).habitat: Dry open plains, scrub woodlands, and ravines across Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, and Bihar.
Palash (Flame of the Forest).active_compounds: Butein, Butin, Butrin, Isobutrin, Coreopsin, Palasonin, Gallic acid
Palash (Flame of the Forest).soil: Saline, alkaline, sodic, and waterlogged clay soils that few other trees can tolerate
Palash (Flame of the Forest).toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; flowers are entirely natural and safe
Palash (Flame of the Forest).uses: Natural chemical-free Holi gulal dye, biodegradable dining leaf plates (Pattal), gum kino resin, and lac insect cultivation host.
Palash (Flame of the Forest).ayurvedic_uses: Seeds (Palash Beeja) are a potent anthelmintic against intestinal tapeworms (Krimighna); flower water cools urinary tract burning and heatstroke.

Babool (Acacia).description: A hardy, thorny multipurpose tree with fine feathery leaves, fragrant yellow pom-pom flowers, and beaded grey seedpods.
Babool (Acacia).habitat: Arid, semi-arid, and wasteland zones across Rajasthan, Punjab, Gujarat, Haryana, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh.
Babool (Acacia).active_compounds: Acacia gum (Arabinogalactan), Tannins, Catechin, Epicatechin, Gallic acid
Babool (Acacia).watering: Low; thrives in arid climates with minimal precipitation
Babool (Acacia).soil: Tolerates black cotton soil, alkaline soils, and dry gravelly ground
Babool (Acacia).toxicity_pets: Pods and leaves non-toxic; sharp thorns represent a physical injury risk
Babool (Acacia).uses: Natural gum arabic extraction, traditional chew-sticks for dental enamel care, high-density firewood, and fencing.
Babool (Acacia).ayurvedic_uses: Bark and tender pods are powerful astringents; treats bleeding gums, stomatitis, chronic diarrhea, and spermatorrhea.

Drumstick (Moringa).description: A fast-growing, slender deciduous tree acclaimed worldwide as a nutritional superfood with nutrient-dense leaves, creamy white flowers, and long fluted pods.
Drumstick (Moringa).habitat: Native to the sub-Himalayan tracts of northwestern India; cultivated in virtually every household garden in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh.
Drumstick (Moringa).active_compounds: Moringine, Pterygospermin, Quercetin, Kaempferol, Chlorogenic acid, Isothiocyanates
Drumstick (Moringa).watering: Low to Moderate; susceptible to waterlogged root rot
Drumstick (Moringa).soil: Well-drained sandy loam or alluvial soil with pH 6.3 - 7.5
Drumstick (Moringa).toxicity_pets: Leaves and pods are safe and healthy; root bark contains toxic alkaloids and should be avoided for pets
Drumstick (Moringa).uses: Nutritional dietary supplement, pods in sambar and curries, seed oil (Ben oil) for cosmetics, and seeds used in natural water purification flocculation.
Drumstick (Moringa).ayurvedic_uses: Deeply penetrating and heating (Ushna Virya); pacifies Vata and Kapha; used for joint arthritis, gout, edema, hypertension, and worm infestations.

regional_names.hindi: कढ़ी पत्ता (Kadhi Patta) / मीठा नीम (Meetha Neem)

Curry Leaf Tree.description: A highly aromatic small evergreen tree or large shrub with glossy dark-green pinnate leaflets that emit a distinctive zesty aroma when bruised.
Curry Leaf Tree.habitat: Wild in the foothills of the Himalayas and deciduous forests of peninsular India; cultivated in home gardens across South India and Gujarat.
Curry Leaf Tree.active_compounds: Mahanimbine, Koenimbine, Girinimbine, Caryophyllene, Pinene, Lutein
Curry Leaf Tree.soil: Fertile, humus-rich, well-draining loamy or red garden soil
Curry Leaf Tree.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe culinary foliage
Curry Leaf Tree.uses: Essential culinary seasoning across Indian cuisine (tadka), herbal hair oils for hair pigmentation, and aromatic soap essences.
Curry Leaf Tree.ayurvedic_uses: Deepana (appetizer) and Pachana (digestive); controls morning sickness, diarrhea, reduces hypercholesterolemia, and prevents premature graying of hair.

Parijat (Night Jasmine Tree).description: A holy small tree or large shrub with rough leaves and nocturnal star-like blossoms featuring pristine white petals and a fiery orange tubular center.
Parijat (Night Jasmine Tree).habitat: Sub-Himalayan tracts, forests of Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, and cultivated near homes and temples across India.
Parijat (Night Jasmine Tree).active_compounds: Nyctanthin, Arbortristoside A & B, Iridoid glucosides, Crocin, Tannins, Beta-sitosterol
Parijat (Night Jasmine Tree).soil: Adaptable to various soils, preferring loamy garden soil with good drainage
Parijat (Night Jasmine Tree).uses: Flowers collected from the ground for worship, delicate saffron-colored cloth dye from flower tubes, and autumn festival celebrations.
Parijat (Night Jasmine Tree).ayurvedic_uses: Leaves are celebrated for treating chronic sciatica (Gridhrasi), severe arthritis, intermittent malaria fevers, and internal worm infestations.

Chinar.description: A magnificent, massive deciduous tree symbolizing the Kashmir valley, famous for its palmate maple-like leaves that turn ablaze with golden, orange, and crimson foliage in autumn.
Chinar.habitat: Kashmir valley, Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and northern temperate hill regions.
Chinar.active_compounds: Platanic acid, Betulinic acid, Quercetin, Kaempferol, Tannins
Chinar.watering: Moderate to High; deep root system absorbs abundant subterranean water
Chinar.soil: Deep, moist, well-drained alluvial and riverine soils of valley floors
Chinar.uses: Iconic cultural heritage of Kashmir, landscape shade in Mughal gardens (Nishat, Shalimar), high-grade wood for Kashmiri papier-mache and wood carving.
Chinar.ayurvedic_uses: Bark astringent used in folk traditions for toothache, blepharitis, and dysentery; leaves boiled in vinegar applied for bruises.

Deodar Cedar.description: A noble, coniferous evergreen tree of the Western Himalayas with sweeping pendulous branchlets, barrel-shaped cones, and aromatic durable wood, worshipped as 'wood of the gods'.
Deodar Cedar.habitat: Western Himalayas across Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Jammu & Kashmir at altitudes of 1,500 to 3,200 meters.
Deodar Cedar.active_compounds: Himachalol, Atlantone, Allohimachalol, Deodardione, Cedrene, Taxifolin
Deodar Cedar.watering: Moderate; adapted to mountain precipitation and winter snow melt
Deodar Cedar.soil: Well-drained rocky, gravelly, or acidic mountain soils
Deodar Cedar.toxicity_pets: Resin and needles may cause stomach irritation if ingested by dogs or cats
Deodar Cedar.uses: High-value structural timber for houseboats in Srinagar, temples, railway ties, and cedarwood essential oil distillation.
Deodar Cedar.ayurvedic_uses: Wood is Snigdha and Ushna; pacifies Vata and Kapha; used for chronic cough, asthma, rheumatism, skin ailments, and filariasis.

Indian Mahogany.description: A tall, handsome deciduous forest tree prized for its lightweight, aromatic, reddish-brown timber that resembles true mahogany.
Indian Mahogany.habitat: Sub-Himalayan valleys, Western Ghats, and moist tropical forests of Assam, Bengal, and Tamil Nadu.
Indian Mahogany.watering: Moderate; requires adequate soil moisture during active growth
Indian Mahogany.soil: Deep, moist, fertile alluvial and red loam soils
Indian Mahogany.uses: Cabinetmaking, musical instruments (sitar, tanpura resonators), cigar boxes, ornamental carving, and avenue planting.
Indian Mahogany.ayurvedic_uses: Bark acts as an astringent and tonic; used for chronic dysentery, wound healing, and menstrual disorders; flowers yield a sulfur-yellow dye.

Mahua.description: An indispensable deciduous forest tree in tribal India, famous for its succulent, sweet, cream-colored flowers and oil-bearing seeds.
Mahua.habitat: Dry deciduous forests of Central and Eastern India, spanning Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Maharashtra.
Mahua.active_compounds: Madhucic acid, Saponins, Beta-amyrin, Lupeol, Quercetin, Stearic acid
Mahua.soil: Tolerates poor rocky, sandy, and lateritic soils
Mahua.toxicity_pets: Flowers non-toxic; seed press-cake has high saponin content and should not be ingested by pets
Mahua.uses: Flowers eaten fresh, dried, or brewed into traditional drinks; seed oil (Mahua butter) used for temple lamps, cooking, and bio-diesel.
Mahua.ayurvedic_uses: Flowers are sweet, cooling demulcent; used for bronchitis, cough, fatigue, and enhancing lactation in nursing mothers.

Khejri.species: Khejri (Ghaf Tree / Golden Tree of the Desert)
Khejri.description: The state tree of Rajasthan, sacred to Bishnoi communities, famed for thriving in harsh Thar Desert sands and enriching arid desert soils.
Khejri.habitat: Arid and semi-arid desert landscapes of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana.
Khejri.active_compounds: Prosogerin A-E, Patulitrin, Rutin, Gallic acid, Beta-sitosterol
Khejri.watering: Very Low; deep taproot penetrates over 30 meters to reach deep subterranean water
Khejri.soil: Hyper-arid, sandy desert dune soils, highly saline and calcareous soils
Khejri.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; pods are a healthy natural desert forage
Khejri.uses: Unripe pods (Sangri) are a culinary delicacy in Rajasthani Panchkuta curry; foliage (Loong) is vital livestock fodder; soil nitrogen stabilization.
Khejri.ayurvedic_uses: Bark and leaves used for rheumatism, skin leprosy, scorpion stings, and miscarriage prevention; revered in religious Shami Pooja.

Lotus (National Flower).description: The National Flower of India, an iconic aquatic plant with radiant pink and white petals and water-repellent leaves that symbolize spiritual purity and detachment.
Lotus (National Flower).habitat: Freshwater lakes, temple tanks, floodplains, and ponds across Jammu & Kashmir (Dal Lake), Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
Lotus (National Flower).active_compounds: Nuciferine, Nelumboside, Roemerine, Quercetin, Kaempferol, Isoquercitrin
Lotus (National Flower).watering: Aquatic; grows rooted in deep pond mud with leaves and flowers floating on the water surface
Lotus (National Flower).soil: Heavy clay, organic muck, or rich lake mud submerged under 30-100 cm of calm water
Lotus (National Flower).toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to dogs and cats; completely benign
Lotus (National Flower).uses: National emblem, temple worship, culinary lotus roots (kamal kakdi) and seeds (makhana / foxnuts), and traditional floral garlands.
Lotus (National Flower).ayurvedic_uses: Pitta-pacifying and cooling; petal decoction soothes burning fevers, heart palpitations, bleeding disorders, and calms mental restlessness.

Marigold.description: A cheerful, aromatic ornamental herb bearing ruffled golden-yellow and vibrant orange pom-pom blossoms that are indispensable in Indian festive celebrations.
Marigold.habitat: Cultivated ubiquitously across farmland, home gardens, and peri-urban tracts in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, and Uttar Pradesh.
Marigold.active_compounds: Lutein, Zeaxanthin, Tagetone, Quercetagetin, Terthienyl, Carotenoids
Marigold.watering: Moderate; water at the base to prevent fungal powdery mildew on blossoms
Marigold.soil: Fertile, well-draining garden loam or sandy loam with pH 6.0 - 7.5
Marigold.toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic to dogs and cats; sap can cause mild dermal irritation and stomach upset if ingested in quantity
Marigold.uses: Religious festival garlands (Diwali, Dussehra), wedding decoration, natural yellow food coloring, companion planting to repel root-knot nematodes.
Marigold.ayurvedic_uses: Leaves and flowers crushed into juice to heal skin ulcers, stop capillary bleeding, cure piles, and soothe insect stings.

Jasmine.description: A vigorous climbing shrub renowned for its intensely fragrant star-shaped white blossoms that perfume the evening air.
Jasmine.habitat: Foothills of the Himalayas, valleys of Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and widely grown in domestic gardens across peninsular India.
Jasmine.active_compounds: Benzyl acetate, Linalool, Jasmone, Methyl jasmonate, Indole, Geraniol
Jasmine.watering: Moderate; requires regular watering during blooming season with good drainage
Jasmine.soil: Rich, well-drained, organically enriched loamy soil
Jasmine.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe around cats and dogs
Jasmine.uses: Luxury perfume attars, Jasmine tea flavoring, traditional bridal garlands, and ornamental garden trellises.
Jasmine.ayurvedic_uses: Cools Pitta and soothes fiery emotions; petal paste cures mouth ulcers (Mukha Paka), eye redness, and headache.

Hibiscus.description: A vibrant tropical evergreen shrub bearing large, trumpet-shaped five-petaled blossoms with prominent projecting staminal columns.
Hibiscus.habitat: Found in domestic gardens, temple courtyards, and urban hedges across tropical and subtropical India.
Hibiscus.active_compounds: Anthocyanins, Hibiscetin, Flavonoids, Mucilage, Quercetin, Malvidin
Hibiscus.watering: Moderate to High; maintain evenly moist soil without waterlogging
Hibiscus.soil: Moist, organically fertile, slightly acidic loamy soil (pH 6.0 - 6.8)
Hibiscus.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to cats and dogs according to ASPCA guidelines
Hibiscus.uses: Sacred offering to Goddess Kali and Lord Ganesha, herbal haircare oil formulations, herbal tea blends, and landscape hedging.
Hibiscus.ayurvedic_uses: Keshya (premier hair growth stimulant); thickens hair follicles, prevents alopecia, lowers blood pressure, and regulates painful menstruation.

Rose.description: A heavily scented, multi-petaled deciduous thorny shrub famed for yielding the finest pure rose water and fragrant attar.
Rose.habitat: Extensively cultivated in Rajasthan (Pushkar, Haldighati), Uttar Pradesh (Kannauj, Aligarh), and Jammu & Kashmir.
Rose.active_compounds: Citronellol, Geraniol, Nerol, Phenylethyl alcohol, Damascenone, Eugenol
Rose.watering: Moderate; deep watering at soil level; avoids sprinkler wetting of petals
Rose.soil: Fertile, clay-loam or well-drained sandy loam rich in compost (pH 6.0 - 7.0)
Rose.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; thorns can cause mechanical scratches
Rose.uses: Rose water (Gulab Jal), culinary Gulkand rose jam, high-end perfumery attar, sweets flavoring, and floral wreaths.
Rose.ayurvedic_uses: Cooling Rasayana; pacifies Pitta; soothes acidity, ulcers, conjunctivitis eye irritation, and acts as a gentle heart and nervous tonic.

Sunflower.description: A striking, tall annual plant topped by a gigantic composite golden-rayed floral head that tracks the sun across the sky via heliotropism.
Sunflower.habitat: Farmed extensively as an oilseed crop in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Punjab, and Haryana.
Sunflower.active_compounds: Linoleic acid, Oleic acid, Alpha-tocopherol (Vitamin E), Helianthic acid, Phytosterols
Sunflower.sunlight: Full Sun (requires 6-8 hours direct unobstructed sunlight)
Sunflower.watering: Moderate; requires regular watering during bud initiation and seed formation
Sunflower.soil: Deep, fertile, well-draining loamy or black cotton soil with pH 6.0 - 7.5
Sunflower.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to dogs, cats, and birds
Sunflower.uses: Commercial edible cooking oil extraction, healthy edible seeds, cut flowers, and wildlife birdfeed.
Sunflower.ayurvedic_uses: Seeds nourish Dhatus and improve stamina; oil used as a lipid base for anti-inflammatory herbal massages; pacifies Vata.

regional_names.hindi: बोगनवेलिया (Bougainvillea) / कागज के फूल (Kagaz ke Phool)

Bougainvillea.description: A vigorous, thorny woody climbing vine known for its exuberant masses of paper-thin, long-lasting bracts in shades of magenta, purple, red, and pink.
Bougainvillea.habitat: Grown across urban boundary walls, bungalow gates, highway median dividers, and pergolas throughout India.
Bougainvillea.active_compounds: Betacyanins, Betanidin, Isobetanidin, Quercetin, Pinitol, Phenolics
Bougainvillea.sunlight: Full Sun (flourishes best in intense heat and solar exposure)
Bougainvillea.watering: Low; drought-tolerant; overwatering reduces flower bract production
Bougainvillea.soil: Well-drained, gritty, sandy, or loamy soil; tolerates poor fertility
Bougainvillea.toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic to pets; ingestion of leaves/bracts can cause mild gastrointestinal upset; thorns cause physical punctures
Bougainvillea.uses: Security fencing, highway sound and dust barrier, vibrant landscaping trellis, and heat-resistant urban greenery.
Bougainvillea.ayurvedic_uses: Bract extracts used in modern ethnopharmacology for anti-diabetic and hepatoprotective properties; leaves used for cough and asthma.

Champa (Plumeria/Frangipani).description: A picturesque succulent-stemmed deciduous small tree with spirally clustered leaves and waxy, spiraling, intensely fragrant white, yellow, or pink flowers.
Champa (Plumeria/Frangipani).habitat: Planted in Buddhist and Hindu temple precincts, parks, and home courtyards throughout tropical India.
Champa (Plumeria/Frangipani).watering: Low to Moderate; thick succulent branches store water; highly rot-prone if waterlogged
Champa (Plumeria/Frangipani).soil: Free-draining sandy loam or cactus mix; thrives in dry soils
Champa (Plumeria/Frangipani).toxicity_pets: Toxic to pets; milky white latex sap contains cardiac glycosides and irritants that cause vomiting and skin blistering
Champa (Plumeria/Frangipani).uses: Temple offerings, aromatic landscaping, fragrant floral garlands, and garden specimen architecture.
Champa (Plumeria/Frangipani).ayurvedic_uses: Bark decoction used as a febrifuge and purgative; flowers used to treat burning sensations and thirst; sap applied to warts.

Night Queen (Raat ki Rani).description: An evergreen woody shrub bearing clusters of slender tubular greenish-white flowers that open after dusk, emitting an intoxicating, far-reaching nocturnal scent.
Night Queen (Raat ki Rani).habitat: Popular across home courtyards, residential boundary borders, and city parks throughout India.
Night Queen (Raat ki Rani).active_compounds: Solasodine, Spirostanol saponins, Cestrumoside, Linalool, Cineole, Flavonoids
Night Queen (Raat ki Rani).watering: Moderate; regular watering during summer blooming season
Night Queen (Raat ki Rani).soil: Moist, rich, well-draining loamy garden soil
Night Queen (Raat ki Rani).toxicity_pets: TOXIC to cats, dogs, and livestock; all plant parts, particularly berries, contain anticholinergic solanaceous saponins
Night Queen (Raat ki Rani).uses: Nocturnal garden fragrance, privacy screening hedge, and ornamental horticulture.
Night Queen (Raat ki Rani).ayurvedic_uses: Leaves historically used in folk healing for epilepsy and spasmodic affections; used with extreme caution due to toxicity.

Mogra (Arabian Jasmine).description: A bushy scrambling shrub producing dense, multi-whorled ivory-white rosettes with an unforgettable, divine sweet fragrance, celebrated in Madurai gajras.
Mogra (Arabian Jasmine).habitat: Cultivated extensively across Madurai (Tamil Nadu - GI Tagged), Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Bengal.
Mogra (Arabian Jasmine).active_compounds: Sambacolignans, Benzyl acetate, Linalool, Indole, Cis-jasmone, Farnesene
Mogra (Arabian Jasmine).watering: Moderate; regular hydration, reduced slightly before pruning to stimulate blooming buds
Mogra (Arabian Jasmine).soil: Fertile, loamy, well-aerated soil enriched with organic cow manure (pH 6.5 - 7.5)
Mogra (Arabian Jasmine).uses: South Indian bridal gajras (hair adornment), deity worship offerings, luxury Jasmine absolute attar, and Jasmine tea flavoring.
Mogra (Arabian Jasmine).ayurvedic_uses: Cooling and pacifying to Pitta; leaf juice applied to breast tissue to suppress excessive lactation; treats mouth sores and nervous stress.

Parijat Flower.description: Delicate five-to-eight petaled nocturnal blossoms with pure porcelain-white petals and a brilliant orange-red tube that drop at dawn onto grass carpets.
Parijat Flower.habitat: Planted widely across residential gardens, public parks, and temple grounds across India; blossoms arrive during autumn (Durga Puja / Navratri).
Parijat Flower.active_compounds: Crocin, Nyctanthin, D-mannitol, Beta-amyrin, Essential fragrance terpenes
Parijat Flower.watering: Moderate; avoid standing water around root zone
Parijat Flower.soil: Well-drained garden loam or alluvial soil
Parijat Flower.uses: The only flower traditionally gathered from the ground for Hindu worship; tubular stalks boiled to create auspicious saffron fabric dye.
Parijat Flower.ayurvedic_uses: Flower infusion acts as a mild sedative, cardiac tonic, and stomachic; relaxes mental anxiety and balances Vata-Pitta.

Kaner (Oleander).description: A tough, evergreen drought-proof shrub producing clusters of striking rose-pink, red, or white pinwheel flowers with narrow leathery leaves.
Kaner (Oleander).habitat: Extensively planted along highway medians, railway embankments, dry hillsides, and temple grounds across India.
Kaner (Oleander).active_compounds: Oleandrin, Folinerin, Digitoxigenin, Neriin, Cardiac glycosides
Kaner (Oleander).sunlight: Full Sun (loves intense solar radiation and heat)
Kaner (Oleander).watering: Low; remarkably drought-hardy and requires minimal moisture once rooted
Kaner (Oleander).soil: Grows in virtually any soil: rocky, saline, sandy, or contaminated roadside soils
Kaner (Oleander).toxicity_pets: HIGHLY TOXIC to dogs, cats, horses, and humans; all parts contain lethal cardiac glycosides that cause arrhythmias and arrest
Kaner (Oleander).uses: Highway median crash and headlight glare barriers, desert landscaping, pollution absorption, and temple offerings to Lord Shiva.
Kaner (Oleander).ayurvedic_uses: Used exclusively externally in classical Ayurveda (Shodhana purified Karavira) in taila (oils) for intractable chronic eczema, scabies, and vitiligo.

Rhododendron.description: The State Tree of Uttarakhand, an alpine woody tree whose scarlet bell-shaped floral trusses ignite Himalayan hillsides into red fire every spring.
Rhododendron.habitat: Himalayan temperate zone across Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh at altitudes between 1,500 and 3,600 meters.
Rhododendron.active_compounds: Rutin, Quercetin, Epicatechin, Hyperoside, Ursolic acid, Cyanidin glycosides
Rhododendron.watering: Moderate; relies on mountain fog, rain, and snow melt
Rhododendron.soil: Acidic, humus-rich, well-draining rocky mountain loam (pH 4.5 - 5.5)
Rhododendron.toxicity_pets: Leaves and honey contain grayanotoxins toxic to pets; flower petal squash consumed safely by humans
Rhododendron.uses: Famous Buransh floral squash/sharbat, local Himalayan wine, ornamental tourism attraction, and fuelwood.
Rhododendron.ayurvedic_uses: Petal juice used as an effective cardiac tonic, anti-hyperglycemic, hepatoprotective, and refresher for mountain altitude sickness.

Orchids.description: An exquisite epiphytic orchid bearing long, drooping, cylindrical inflorescences densely packed with over 100 spotted pink-and-white fragrant blossoms.
Orchids.habitat: Canopies of tropical trees in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Western Ghats, and the Andaman Islands; state flower of Assam.
Orchids.sunlight: Bright, indirect filtered sunlight; scorches under direct mid-day sun
Orchids.watering: Moderate; requires high atmospheric humidity (70-80%) and rapid aerial root drying
Orchids.soil: Epiphytic; grows on tree bark or coarse coconut husk, charcoal, and orchid fir chips
Orchids.uses: Traditional hair adornment by Assamese dancers during the Rongali Bihu festival, high-value ornamental collectible, and floral bio-indicator.
Orchids.ayurvedic_uses: Roots used in folk medicine for rheumatism, wound healing, earache drops, and alleviating menstrual irregularities.

Chrysanthemum.description: A bushy perennial floriferous herb with deeply lobed leaves and abundant multi-petaled flowerheads in dazzling yellows, purples, and whites.
Chrysanthemum.habitat: Widely cultivated across Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Bengal as a major winter floral crop.
Chrysanthemum.active_compounds: Chrysanthemin, Luteolin, Apigenin, Acacetin, Camphor, Borneol, Chlorogenic acid
Chrysanthemum.watering: Moderate; keep root zone evenly moist without splashing flower petals
Chrysanthemum.soil: Rich, well-aerated sandy loam with compost (pH 6.5 - 7.0)
Chrysanthemum.toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic to cats and dogs; contains pyrethrins causing salivation, vomiting, and diarrhea if eaten in large amounts
Chrysanthemum.uses: Commercial cut flowers, garlands for temple pooja, winter garden border bedding, and herbal tea infusions.
Chrysanthemum.ayurvedic_uses: Cooling flower infusion pacifies Pitta; soothes conjunctivitis, headaches, hypertension, and skin inflammations.

Daisy.description: A low-growing herbaceous perennial with rosettes of spoon-shaped leaves and charming composite blossoms with yellow central discs and white rays.
Daisy.habitat: Hill stations and temperate gardens across Shimla, Ooty, Darjeeling, Kodaikanal, and winter plains across North India.
Daisy.active_compounds: Bellisaponins, Polyacetylenes, Flavonoids, Apigenin, Triterpenoids, Inulin
Daisy.watering: Moderate; needs consistently moist soil in cool microclimates
Daisy.soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-draining garden soil
Daisy.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets according to veterinary registers
Daisy.uses: Winter bedding displays, rock gardens, border borders, children's daisy chains, and ornamental potting.
Daisy.ayurvedic_uses: Known as a traditional vulnerary herb; applied topically to heal bruises, contusions, and aching muscular joints.

Dahlia.description: A tuberous herbaceous perennial celebrated for its enormous, spectacular geometric blooms ranging from miniature pom-poms to giant dinner-plate varieties.
Dahlia.habitat: Grown in winter gardens across the northern plains and year-round in hill stations like Kalimpong, Bangalore, and Pune.
Dahlia.active_compounds: Inulin (in tubers), Anthocyanins, Butein, Flavonoids, Polysaccharides
Dahlia.watering: Moderate to High; deep soaking during budding; tubers rot if sitting in stagnant mud
Dahlia.toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic to cats and dogs; can cause mild gastrointestinal irritation and dermal dermatitis
Dahlia.uses: Premier winter flower show exhibit, luxurious floral centerpieces, landscape beds, and commercial cut flowers.
Dahlia.ayurvedic_uses: Tubers rich in inulin used as a prebiotic source; petal extracts demonstrate strong free radical scavenging.

Lily.description: A noble bulbous perennial producing tall leafy stems crowned by pure alabaster-white trumpet blossoms with golden-yellow anthers and sweet perfume.
Lily.habitat: Cultivated in temperate hill resorts of Nilgiris, Kashmir, Uttarakhand, and greenhouse floriculture around Pune and Bengaluru.
Lily.active_compounds: Lilaline, Jatropham, Steroidal saponins, Quercetin, Flavonoids
Lily.sunlight: Full Sun to Partial Shade (roots prefer shaded, cool mulch)
Lily.watering: Moderate; keep root bulb zone evenly moist without saturation
Lily.soil: Fertile, humus-rich, porous, well-draining loamy soil
Lily.toxicity_pets: FATAL TO CATS; true lilies cause severe, acute renal failure in feline pets from even minor pollen ingestion
Lily.uses: High-end florist arrangements, wedding décor, religious altars, and luxury courtyard horticulture.
Lily.ayurvedic_uses: Bulb paste applied externally for burns, softening inflammatory boils, and soothing heated skin eruptions.

Tube Rose (Rajnigandha).description: A fragrant bulbous perennial producing erect flower spikes up to a meter high packed with pure waxy-white florets that emanate powerful night scent.
Tube Rose (Rajnigandha).habitat: Commercially farmed on vast acreage in West Bengal (Ranaghat), Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra (Pune), and Karnataka.
Tube Rose (Rajnigandha).active_compounds: Methyl benzoate, Methyl anthranilate, Benzyl alcohol, Eugenol, Geraniol, Nerol
Tube Rose (Rajnigandha).watering: Moderate; regular watering during summer spike formation; avoid water stagnation
Tube Rose (Rajnigandha).soil: Rich, well-drained sandy loam or clay loam rich in compost (pH 6.5 - 7.5)
Tube Rose (Rajnigandha).toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic to pets; bulbs contain saponins that can cause vomiting if chewed
Tube Rose (Rajnigandha).uses: Wedding garlands, floral bouquets, deity adoration, and extraction of prized tuberose concrete absolute for luxury perfumes.
Tube Rose (Rajnigandha).ayurvedic_uses: Calming to the nervous system; soothes emotional stress, pacifies Vata, and acts as an aphrodisiac Rasayana.

regional_names.hindi: टेसू के फूल (Tesu ke Phool) / पलाश पुष्प (Palash Pushpa)

Palash Flower.description: Beak-shaped velvety bright orange-red blossoms produced in dense masses on leafless branches in spring, resembling a forest canopy on fire.
Palash Flower.habitat: Dry open forests and agricultural borders of Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Rajasthan.
Palash Flower.active_compounds: Butrin, Isobutrin, Butein, Coreopsin, Flavonoids, Chalcones
Palash Flower.watering: Low; natural monsoonal rains suffice for the parent tree
Palash Flower.soil: Tolerant of saline, alkaline, and heavy clay wastelands
Palash Flower.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; entirely edible natural organic blossom
Palash Flower.uses: Traditional herbal chemical-free Holi gulal dye, sacred worship of Goddess Saraswati, and fabric dyeing.
Palash Flower.ayurvedic_uses: Flowers soaked in water overnight produce a cooling bath that relieves heatstroke, prickly heat, and burning micturition in summer.

Gulmohar Flower.description: Large scarlet to orange-vermilion flowers with five spreading petals, one of which is splashed and streaked with white and yellow called the 'standard'.
Gulmohar Flower.habitat: Avenues, campuses, and parks in every Indian state during the summer months of April to June.
Gulmohar Flower.watering: Low; abundant blooms occur after a dry winter spell
Gulmohar Flower.soil: Adaptable to various soils with good drainage
Gulmohar Flower.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; safe if petals fall on lawns
Gulmohar Flower.uses: Spectacular summer landscaping, floral photography, avenue decoration, and botanical education.
Gulmohar Flower.ayurvedic_uses: Folk medicine uses petal infusions for reducing fevers, relieving body heat, and alleviating joint inflammation.

Butterfly Pea (Aparajita).description: A graceful perennial twining vine bearing striking cobalt-blue flowers with a white-and-yellow throat that resemble a conch shell.
Butterfly Pea (Aparajita).habitat: Climbing fences, hedgerows, and trellises across Uttar Pradesh, Bengal, Kerala, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu.
Butterfly Pea (Aparajita).active_compounds: Ternatins (delphinidin anthocyanins), Taraxerol, Kaempferol, Cyclotides, Quercetin
Butterfly Pea (Aparajita).soil: Rich, well-draining garden loam; fixes atmospheric nitrogen to enrich soil
Butterfly Pea (Aparajita).toxicity_pets: Seeds can cause vomiting if swallowed in bulk; flowers are non-toxic and edible
Butterfly Pea (Aparajita).uses: Sacred offering to Lord Shiva and Goddess Durga, natural blue herbal tea (which turns purple with lemon), and culinary food dye.
Butterfly Pea (Aparajita).ayurvedic_uses: Medhya Rasayana (brain memory enhancer); pacifies Tridosha; relieves anxiety, enhances cognitive retention, and improves vision.

Crape Jasmine (Chandni).description: A handsome evergreen shrub featuring glossy dark green foliage and pristine white pinwheel-shaped flowers with ruffled petal edges.
Crape Jasmine (Chandni).habitat: Planted in virtually every home garden, park hedge, and temple courtyard across tropical and subtropical India.
Crape Jasmine (Chandni).watering: Moderate; keep soil slightly moist during hot dry periods
Crape Jasmine (Chandni).toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic to pets; milky sap contains alkaloids that can irritate the mouth and stomach
Crape Jasmine (Chandni).uses: Temple pooja worship flowers, landscape hedging, night-shining white garden borders, and ornamental shrubbery.
Crape Jasmine (Chandni).ayurvedic_uses: Milky sap mixed with oil applied for soothing inflamed eyes and opacities; root chewed for toothache; cools excessive Pitta.

Sadabahar (Periwinkle).description: An evergreen subshrub blooming continuously year-round with glossy oval leaves and five-petaled salverform pink or white flowers.
Sadabahar (Periwinkle).habitat: Abundantly naturalized along roadsides, dry wastelands, and grown in pots and gardens across all states of India.
Sadabahar (Periwinkle).active_compounds: Vincristine, Vinblastine, Ajmalicine, Serpentine, Catharanthine, Vindoline
Sadabahar (Periwinkle).watering: Low; remarkably drought-proof; vulnerable to fungal root rot if overwatered
Sadabahar (Periwinkle).soil: Poor, sandy, or rocky well-drained soils; thrives where other flowers perish
Sadabahar (Periwinkle).toxicity_pets: TOXIC to cats and dogs; contains cytotoxic vinca alkaloids that cause hypotension, lethargy, and neurotoxicity if consumed
Sadabahar (Periwinkle).uses: Source of pharmaceutical anticancer drugs (vincristine & vinblastine), year-round ornamental garden borders, and butterfly nectar.
Sadabahar (Periwinkle).ayurvedic_uses: Leaf juice traditionally consumed in folk medicine for managing diabetes mellitus (Madhumeha) and regulating high blood pressure.

Brahma Kamal.description: The State Flower of Uttarakhand, a mythical alpine sacred herb blooming at night with chartreuse papery bracts enclosing purple flowerheads.
Brahma Kamal.habitat: High-altitude Himalayan screes and rocky slopes between 3,500 and 4,800 meters in Kedarnath, Hemkund Sahib, and Valley of Flowers.
Brahma Kamal.active_compounds: Sesquiterpene lactones, Flavonoids, Syringin, Quercetin, Rutin
Brahma Kamal.sunlight: Full alpine sun with cold high-altitude winds
Brahma Kamal.watering: Adapted to sub-zero snow melt and mist; difficult to cultivate in warm plains
Brahma Kamal.soil: Alpine rocky scree, gravel, and acidic glacial moraine soils
Brahma Kamal.uses: Offered reverently at high Himalayan shrines (Badrinath, Kedarnath), cultural heritage icon, and Himalayan conservation flagship.
Brahma Kamal.ayurvedic_uses: Used in Tibetan and Himalayan traditional medicine for bone fractures, internal wounds, urinary disorders, and reproductive health.

Mango (King of Fruits).description: The quintessential tropical summer fruit of India, celebrated for its succulent, sweet, aromatic golden pulp in world-famous varieties like Alphonso, Dasheri, and Kesar.
Mango (King of Fruits).habitat: Major fruit orchards across Uttar Pradesh (Malihabad), Maharashtra (Ratnagiri), Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, and Bihar.
Mango (King of Fruits).active_compounds: Mangiferin, Beta-carotene, Cryptoxanthin, Ascorbic acid, Gallic acid, Quercetin
Mango (King of Fruits).watering: Moderate; deep irrigation during fruit swelling, ceased right before harvest to enhance brix sugar content
Mango (King of Fruits).soil: Deep, fertile alluvial or rich loamy soil with excellent drainage (pH 5.5 - 7.5)
Mango (King of Fruits).toxicity_pets: Fruit flesh is safe; seed kernel is a choking hazard and contains small amounts of cyanide compounds
Mango (King of Fruits).uses: Eaten fresh, mango lassi, aamras, mango shakes, raw mango pickles (achaar), aam panna summer cooler, and export fruit.
Mango (King of Fruits).ayurvedic_uses: Ripe sweet mango builds Dhatus (nourishing Rasayana), boosts vitality, increases Ojas, and balances Vata and Pitta.

Banana.description: A giant herbaceous perennial producing heavy drooping infructescences packed with energy-rich, potassium-loaded yellow finger fruits.
Banana.habitat: Cultivated year-round across Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra (Jalgaon - Banana City), Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, and Kerala.
Banana.active_compounds: Potassium, Vitamin B6, Dopamine, Fructooligosaccharides, Resistant starch, Tryptophan
Banana.watering: High; requires consistently moist, highly aerated soil and abundant hydration
Banana.soil: Rich, deeply fertile, well-draining organic loamy soil with pH 6.0 - 7.5
Banana.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to dogs and cats; a healthy treat in moderation
Banana.uses: Table dessert fruit, raw banana chips, steamed curry, traditional feast dining on fresh green banana leaves, and pseudo-stem fiber crafting.
Banana.ayurvedic_uses: Ripe fruit pacifies Vata and Pitta; strengthens muscle tissue; raw green banana soothes peptic ulcers, acid reflux, and stops diarrhea.

Papaya.description: A fast-growing, large herbaceous tree-like plant with crown-clustered palmate leaves and large oval fruits bearing soft, sweet orange-red pulp.
Papaya.habitat: Grown in backyards and commercial orchards across Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, and West Bengal.
Papaya.active_compounds: Papain (proteolytic enzyme), Chymopapain, Carpaine, Beta-carotene, Lycopene, Vitamin C
Papaya.watering: Moderate; highly sensitive to standing water which causes rapid root collar rot
Papaya.soil: Light, well-draining, organically rich sandy loam (pH 6.0 - 7.0)
Papaya.toxicity_pets: Fruit flesh is safe; seeds are bitter and should be removed before feeding pets
Papaya.uses: Fresh breakfast fruit, digestive fruit salads, tenderizing meat marinade (via papain enzyme), and raw papaya cooked in curries.
Papaya.ayurvedic_uses: Papaya leaf juice is clinically recognized in India for rapidly raising blood platelet counts during Dengue fever; fruit aids digestion and clears intestinal worms.

Guava (Amrood).description: A hardy small tree with smooth copper bark and round green fruits filled with sweet, fragrant white or pink pulp studded with crunchy seeds.
Guava (Amrood).habitat: Thrives across Uttar Pradesh (famous Allahabad Safeda), Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh.
Guava (Amrood).active_compounds: Ascorbic acid (4x higher than orange), Lycopene, Quercetin, Guaijaverin, Dietary pectin
Guava (Amrood).watering: Low to Moderate; extremely resilient to drought and heatwaves
Guava (Amrood).soil: Adaptable to heavy clay, sandy loam, and moderately alkaline soils (pH 5.5 - 8.2)
Guava (Amrood).toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe fruit treat
Guava (Amrood).uses: Eaten raw with black salt and chili powder, guava jelly, canned pulp, and fruit chaat.
Guava (Amrood).ayurvedic_uses: Leaves chewed to immediately cure toothache, mouth ulcers, and inflamed bleeding gums; fruit regulates bowel movement and reduces blood sugar.

Pomegranate (Anaar).description: A spiny deciduous shrub bearing crown-topped leathery red fruits packed with jewel-like crimson arils bursting with sweet-tart antioxidant juice.
Pomegranate (Anaar).habitat: Dry and semi-arid tracts of Maharashtra (Solapur - Bhagwa variety), Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Karnataka.
Pomegranate (Anaar).active_compounds: Punicalagin, Ellagic acid, Punicic acid (conjugated linolenic acid), Anthocyanins, Gallic acid
Pomegranate (Anaar).watering: Low to Moderate; thrives in hot, dry climates; irregular watering causes fruit cracking
Pomegranate (Anaar).soil: Deep, well-draining loamy or light sandy soil (pH 6.5 - 7.5)
Pomegranate (Anaar).toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; seeds are digestible in small quantities for pets
Pomegranate (Anaar).uses: Fresh juice, arils over salads, dried seeds used as sour spice (Anardana) in North Indian cooking, and natural rind tanning dyes.
Pomegranate (Anaar).ayurvedic_uses: Revered as Hridya (heart tonic) and Raktavardhaka (boosts hemoglobin in anemia); Dadimashthaka churna cures amoebic dysentery and hyperacidity.

Apple (Himalayan).description: A temperate deciduous orchard tree producing crisp, juicy red and golden pome fruits that form the economic backbone of Himalayan horticulture.
Apple (Himalayan).habitat: High-altitude temperate hill valleys of Himachal Pradesh (Kinnaur, Shimla, Kullu), Jammu & Kashmir (Shopian, Sopore), and Uttarakhand.
Apple (Himalayan).active_compounds: Quercetin, Phloridzin, Chlorogenic acid, Catechin, Soluble pectin fiber, Ursolic acid
Apple (Himalayan).watering: Moderate; relies on winter snow dormancy and spring-summer mountain rains
Apple (Himalayan).soil: Deep, well-aerated, loamy soil rich in organic matter (pH 6.0 - 6.8)
Apple (Himalayan).toxicity_pets: Flesh is healthy and safe; seeds contain amygdalin (cyanogenic glycoside) and must be discarded
Apple (Himalayan).uses: Fresh table fruit, Apple cider vinegar, dried apple chips, fruit jams, and bakery pies.
Apple (Himalayan).ayurvedic_uses: Cools Pitta and cleanses the digestive tract; increases longevity and physical strength; balances digestive agni when cooked with spices.

Litchi.description: A handsome dense-foliaged evergreen tree producing clusters of strawberry-red bumpy fruits enclosing sweet, translucent, rose-scented aril pulp.
Litchi.habitat: Concentrated in Muzaffarpur (Bihar - famous GI Tagged Shahi Litchi), West Bengal, Uttarakhand (Dehradun), and Punjab.
Litchi.active_compounds: Oligonol, Ascorbic acid, Epicatechin, Rutin, Proanthocyanidins, Potassium
Litchi.watering: High; requires abundant irrigation during flowering and fruit development; sensitive to frost and dry scorching winds
Litchi.soil: Deep, fertile alluvial loam rich in organic matter with accessible water table
Litchi.toxicity_pets: Pulp safe; large glossy brown seed is a choking hazard and contains hypochlorite-like toxic metabolites
Litchi.uses: Fresh summer dessert fruit, litchi juice, canned fruit in syrup, and litchi honey from flower nectar.
Litchi.ayurvedic_uses: Cooling and rejuvenating; replenishes body fluids during scorching summers; nourishes Pitta and quenches excessive thirst.

Chikoo (Sapodilla).description: A sturdy evergreen tree with leathery glossy leaves and round, rough brown-skinned fruits with delightfully grainy, sweet brown-sugar malt flavored pulp.
Chikoo (Sapodilla).habitat: Major coastal production belts in Maharashtra (Dahanu - Gholvad), Gujarat (Valsad), Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
Chikoo (Sapodilla).active_compounds: Tannins, Dietary fiber, Sucrose, Fructose, Gallic acid, Catechin, Vitamin A
Chikoo (Sapodilla).watering: Moderate; highly tolerant of coastal salt spray and dry intervals
Chikoo (Sapodilla).soil: Deep sandy loam, alluvium, or black soil with good drainage
Chikoo (Sapodilla).toxicity_pets: Pulp safe; black shiny seeds have tiny hooks that can lodge in pet intestinal tracts
Chikoo (Sapodilla).uses: Fresh fruit, thick milkshakes, chikoo halwa, fruit ice creams, and chicle latex historically extracted for chewing gum.
Chikoo (Sapodilla).ayurvedic_uses: High tannin content makes decoction of young fruits anti-diarrheal; ripe fruit is an energy-giving Rasayana that soothes gastric mucosal inflammation.

Custard Apple (Sitaphal).description: A small deciduous semi-wild tree bearing knobby, greenish-grey segmented fruits filled with creamy, fragrant, velvety-sweet custard pulp.
Custard Apple (Sitaphal).habitat: Grows wild on rocky hillsides and farmed across Maharashtra (Aurangabad), Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Madhya Pradesh.
Custard Apple (Sitaphal).active_compounds: Annonacin, Acetogenins, Squamocin, Magnesium, Potassium, Vitamin C
Custard Apple (Sitaphal).watering: Low; exceptionally hardy, thrives in drought-prone degraded wastelands
Custard Apple (Sitaphal).soil: Stony, rocky, shallow, and poor gravelly soils; refuses waterlogged soil
Custard Apple (Sitaphal).toxicity_pets: Fruit pulp safe; SEEDS ARE TOXIC to pets and humans; contain neurotoxic annonacin and insecticidal alkaloids
Custard Apple (Sitaphal).uses: Fresh autumn dessert fruit, artisanal Sitaphal ice cream, basundi, fruit milkshakes, and crushed seeds used as organic head lice repellent.
Custard Apple (Sitaphal).ayurvedic_uses: Cooling and nourishing tonic; increases body weight, strengthens cardiac muscle, and pacifies excess Pitta and Vata.

Jackfruit.description: The largest tree-borne fruit in the world, with a green spiky exterior protecting hundreds of sweet, golden bulbs with a unique tropical aroma.
Jackfruit.habitat: The Western Ghats of Kerala and Karnataka, coastal Konkan, West Bengal, Assam, and Tripura.
Jackfruit.active_compounds: Artocarpin, Jacalin, Carotenoids, Dietary fiber, Potassium, Flavonoids
Jackfruit.watering: Moderate; thrives in high monsoonal rainfall zones
Jackfruit.soil: Deep, moisture-retaining but free-draining alluvial or red laterite soils
Jackfruit.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; cooked seeds are safe; raw seeds are hard and can choke pets
Jackfruit.uses: Green raw bulbs cooked as plant-based 'vegetable meat', ripe golden bulbs eaten fresh or made into jackfruit chips (chakkavaratty), and roasted seeds.
Jackfruit.ayurvedic_uses: Ripe fruit is a powerhouse of energy that builds Ojas and muscle tissue; unripe fruit has a low glycemic index and helps regulate blood sugar.

Coconut.description: A fibrous drupe fruit whose green tender form provides sterile electrolyte-packed refreshing water, and whose mature brown form provides rich white copra meat and oil.
Coconut.habitat: Abundant throughout coastal Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Maharashtra, and Odisha.
Coconut.active_compounds: Lauric acid, Capric acid, Monolaurin, Cytokinins, Potassium, Electrolytes
Coconut.watering: High; requires ample humidity and consistent soil hydration
Coconut.soil: Coastal sands, alluvial loams, and red gravelly laterites with good drainage
Coconut.toxicity_pets: Meat and water are non-toxic in small portions; large husk pieces can cause intestinal blockage
Coconut.uses: Tender coconut water (Daab), culinary grated coconut for curries and chutneys, cold-pressed virgin coconut oil, and sacred Hindu temple rituals.
Coconut.ayurvedic_uses: Narikela Udaka is sheetala (cooling), balances Pitta and Vata, treats urinary burning, dehydration, acid peptic disorders, and replenishes vital Ojas.

Watermelon.description: A sprawling trailing annual vine bearing huge spherical or oblong fruits with smooth green rinds and sweet, crisp, crimson flesh that is 92% refreshing water.
Watermelon.habitat: Grown along sandy riverbeds (Diara land) of the Ganges, Yamuna, Godavari, and Krishna rivers during spring and early summer.
Watermelon.active_compounds: Lycopene (higher than raw tomatoes), Citrulline (nitric oxide precursor), Beta-carotene, Cucurbitacin E
Watermelon.watering: Moderate; deep watering while vine spreads and fruit swells; reduced near maturity to sweeten sugars
Watermelon.soil: Warm, sandy riverbed loam with excellent drainage (pH 6.0 - 6.8)
Watermelon.toxicity_pets: Flesh is safe and hydrating for dogs; seeds and tough rind should be avoided to prevent choking
Watermelon.uses: Summer hydration fruit, fresh fruit juices, fruit salads, and roasted nutritious watermelon seeds (magaz).
Watermelon.ayurvedic_uses: Sheetala (cooling) and Mutrala (diuretic); pacifies Pitta, relieves extreme summer heatstroke, flushed kidneys, and soothes urinary tract burning.

Mosambi (Sweet Lime).description: A small citrus tree with thorny branches bearing smooth, greenish-yellow globose fruits renowned for mild, sweet, low-acid refreshing juice.
Mosambi (Sweet Lime).habitat: Major citrus belts of Maharashtra (Jalna, Aurangabad), Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Punjab.
Mosambi (Sweet Lime).active_compounds: Hesperidin, Naringin, Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C), Limonene, Pectin, Flavonoids
Mosambi (Sweet Lime).watering: Moderate; regular irrigation with distinct dry spell before flowering
Mosambi (Sweet Lime).soil: Well-drained light loamy or black cotton soils with good subsoil drainage (pH 6.5 - 7.5)
Mosambi (Sweet Lime).toxicity_pets: Pulp safe in tiny amounts; citrus peels, seeds, and essential oils are toxic to dogs and cats (contains limonene and psoralens)
Mosambi (Sweet Lime).uses: Premier street-side pressed fresh fruit juice in India, hospital convalescent beverage, and fruit salads.
Mosambi (Sweet Lime).ayurvedic_uses: Easily digestible and deeply rejuvenating for recovering patients; alleviates nausea, quenches fever thirst, and stimulates appetite without aggravating Pitta.

Nagpur Orange (Santra).description: A small thorny citrus tree producing loose-skinned, easily peeled bright orange mandarins with a famous sweet-tart flavor profile.
Nagpur Orange (Santra).habitat: The Vidarbha region of Maharashtra (Nagpur - Orange City), Madhya Pradesh, and Darjeeling hills.
Nagpur Orange (Santra).active_compounds: Hesperidin, Tangeretin, Nobiletin, Beta-cryptoxanthin, Ascorbic acid, Limonene
Nagpur Orange (Santra).watering: Moderate; systematic irrigation during fruit development
Nagpur Orange (Santra).soil: Deep, well-aerated black cotton soil or fertile alluvial loam with good drainage
Nagpur Orange (Santra).toxicity_pets: Pulp is safe in moderation; peel and seeds contain citrus oils irritating to pet stomachs
Nagpur Orange (Santra).uses: Table fruit, orange juice, marmalade, candied peel, and orange peel oil in aromatherapy and cosmetics.
Nagpur Orange (Santra).ayurvedic_uses: Deepana (digestive stimulant) and Hridya (heart tonic); pacifies Vata, improves taste perception (Rochaka), and relieves physical fatigue.

Grape.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine trained on overhead pergolas or bower trellises, yielding heavy clusters of sweet, juicy green or black berries.
Grape.habitat: Major commercial viticulture center of Maharashtra (Nashik - Wine Capital of India, Sangli, Pune) and Karnataka.
Grape.active_compounds: Resveratrol, Proanthocyanidins, Quercetin, Tartaric acid, Catechins, Anthocyanins
Grape.watering: Moderate; strictly regulated drip irrigation; water withheld prior to harvest to concentrate sugars
Grape.soil: Well-drained sandy loam, gravelly, or light black soil with pH 6.5 - 7.5
Grape.toxicity_pets: HIGHLY TOXIC TO DOGS AND CATS; even small quantities of grapes or raisins cause acute, irreversible renal failure in canines
Grape.uses: Table fruit, dried raisins (Kishmish), commercial winemaking, and grapeseed oil extraction.
Grape.ayurvedic_uses: Revered in Charaka Samhita as the finest among all fruits (Phalottama); Draksharishta builds hemoglobin, calms Rakta-Pitta, and cures chronic debility.

Jamun Fruit.description: Oblong, glossy deep-violet or black berries with rich magenta juicy pulp that possesses a distinctively sweet, mildly astringent flavor that stains the tongue.
Jamun Fruit.habitat: Common seasonal summer fruit found along roadsides and orchards across Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, and South India.
Jamun Fruit.active_compounds: Anthocyanins (delphinidin, petunidin), Ellagic acid, Jamboline, Gallic acid, Vitamin C
Jamun Fruit.soil: Adaptable to various soils, even moisture-rich soils
Jamun Fruit.toxicity_pets: Pulp safe; hard central pits must not be swallowed by pets
Jamun Fruit.uses: Fresh seasonal fruit eaten with rock salt, Jamun vinegar for diabetic health, Jamun fruit squashes, and artisanal jams.
Jamun Fruit.ayurvedic_uses: Kashaya (astringent) and Madhura (sweet); celebrated for controlling polyuria, regulating blood sugar levels in diabetes, and cooling liver heat.

Amla Fruit.description: Round, segmented, light greenish-yellow translucent fruits legendary for their intensely sour, bitter, astringent first taste followed by a sweet aftertaste.
Amla Fruit.habitat: Commercial orchards and forests across Uttar Pradesh (Pratapgarh), Gujarat, and Tamil Nadu.
Amla Fruit.active_compounds: Heat-stable Ascorbic acid, Tannoid complexes, Emblicanin A & B, Ellagitannins, Chebulinic acid
Amla Fruit.soil: Well-drained loamy, alluvial, or sodic-alkaline soils
Amla Fruit.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe antioxidant fruit
Amla Fruit.uses: Chyawanprash primary ingredient, sweet Murabba, salted Amla candy, pickles, raw juice, and Ayurvedic hair conditioning masks.
Amla Fruit.ayurvedic_uses: Possesses five of the six tastes (lacks only Lavana/salty); supreme anti-aging Rasayana; balances Tridosha, improves eyesight, and enhances immunity.

Tamarind Fruit.description: Brittle brown curved pod fruits enclosing sticky, fibrous, reddish-brown tart pulp packed with hard, glossy brown seeds.
Tamarind Fruit.habitat: Harvested massively across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh.
Tamarind Fruit.active_compounds: Tartaric acid (up to 18%), Potassium bitartrate, Pectin, Invert sugars, Lupeol
Tamarind Fruit.soil: Porous alluvial, sandy, or red loamy soil
Tamarind Fruit.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; high acidity can cause stomach upset if consumed in bulk
Tamarind Fruit.uses: Core culinary souring ingredient in South Indian rasam, sambar, puliyodarai, North Indian imli chutney, and brass metal polish.
Tamarind Fruit.ayurvedic_uses: Deepana (appetizer); stimulates salivary and gastric secretions; relieves anorexia; ripe pulp acts as a gentle, natural laxative.

Fig (Anjeer).description: A small deciduous tree or large shrub yielding teardrop-shaped syconium fruits with green-to-purple skin and soft, sweet, seed-studded pink pulp.
Fig (Anjeer).habitat: Cultivated commercially in Pune (Purandar - GI Tagged Anjeer), Aurangabad, and parts of Karnataka and Gujarat.
Fig (Anjeer).active_compounds: Ficin (proteolytic enzyme), Furocoumarins, Invert sugars, Calcium, Iron, Soluble fiber
Fig (Anjeer).watering: Low to Moderate; sensitive to excessive rainfall during fruit ripening which causes fruit split
Fig (Anjeer).soil: Well-drained, light, calcareous or rich loamy soil (pH 6.5 - 8.0)
Fig (Anjeer).toxicity_pets: Flesh safe in small bites; ficin and furocoumarins in plant sap and green leaves can irritate pet mouths
Fig (Anjeer).uses: Fresh dessert fruit, sun-dried round flattened figs strung on ropes, fig barfi sweets, and high-fiber digestive snacks.
Fig (Anjeer).ayurvedic_uses: Nourishing, Pitta-Vata pacifying tonic; soaked dried figs cure chronic constipation, relieve piles, boost stamina, and purify blood.

Pineapple.description: A tropical terrestrial monocot herb with spiky sword-shaped leaves producing a large, crown-topped composite syncarp fruit with juicy, aromatic yellow flesh.
Pineapple.habitat: Assam, Tripura, Meghalaya, West Bengal (Siliguri - Vazhakulam Queen pineapple), and Kerala.
Pineapple.active_compounds: Bromelain (proteolytic enzyme complex), Ascorbic acid, Manganese, Beta-carotene, Polyphenols
Pineapple.watering: Low to Moderate; thick succulent leaves trap and absorb humidity and dew
Pineapple.soil: Well-drained, mildly acidic sandy loam or lateritic soil (pH 4.5 - 5.5)
Pineapple.toxicity_pets: Pulp safe in moderation; spiky rough rind and central fibrous core can cause intestinal obstruction
Pineapple.uses: Fresh fruit, pineapple juice, tropical fruit chaat, canned slices, tarts, and bromelain enzyme extraction for pharmaceuticals.
Pineapple.ayurvedic_uses: Stimulates weak digestive agni; breaks down sluggish intestinal proteins; relieves systemic inflammatory swelling and sinusitis.

Dragon Fruit (Kamalam).description: A climbing epiphytic cactus producing large, nocturnal flowers and striking bright pink, leather-scaled fruits containing sweet white or magenta flesh with tiny black seeds.
Dragon Fruit (Kamalam).habitat: Rapidly expanding commercial cultivation across Gujarat (renamed Kamalam by state), Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Rajasthan wastelands.
Dragon Fruit (Kamalam).active_compounds: Betalains, Betacyanins, Lycopene, Vitamin C, Dietary fiber, Essential fatty acids in seeds
Dragon Fruit (Kamalam).watering: Very Low; typical desert cactus needs; easily destroyed by root waterlogging
Dragon Fruit (Kamalam).soil: Free-draining sandy loam, rocky, or gravelly soil enriched with organic compost (pH 5.5 - 6.5)
Dragon Fruit (Kamalam).toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to cats and dogs; safe fruit flesh
Dragon Fruit (Kamalam).uses: Gourmet fruit platters, smoothies, fruit bowls, commercial wasteland cultivation, and natural food coloring.
Dragon Fruit (Kamalam).ayurvedic_uses: Cooling, Pitta-pacifying fruit; rich in natural antioxidants; supports cardiovascular health and manages insulin sensitivity.

regional_names.tamil: விளிம்பி பழம் (Vilimbi pazham) / நட்சத்திர பழம் (Star fruit)

Starfruit (Kamrakh).description: A small multi-branched tropical tree producing distinctive five-ridged oblong translucent yellow fruits that display a perfect star shape when sliced crosswise.
Starfruit (Kamrakh).habitat: Grown in home gardens and roadside orchards across Assam, West Bengal, Kerala, and the Konkan coast.
Starfruit (Kamrakh).active_compounds: Oxalic acid, Caramboxin, Ascorbic acid, Epicatechin, Gallic acid, Beta-carotene
Starfruit (Kamrakh).watering: Moderate to High; prefers moist tropical humid surroundings
Starfruit (Kamrakh).soil: Fertile, moist, well-draining acidic or neutral loam
Starfruit (Kamrakh).toxicity_pets: TOXIC TO PETS WITH RENAL DYSFUNCTION; high oxalate and caramboxin content can cause neurotoxicity and kidney stones
Starfruit (Kamrakh).uses: Street-side spicy fruit chaat with black salt, spicy pickles, chutneys, decorative cocktail garnishes, and sweet fruit preserve.
Starfruit (Kamrakh).ayurvedic_uses: Appetizer (Ruchya); quenches intense summer thirst; ripe sweet fruit soothes fevers, while sour fruit treats bilious vomiting.

Bael (Golden Apple).description: A sacred deciduous spiny tree bearing large, round, woody-shelled fruits packed with intensely aromatic, sweet, viscous orange pulp and mucilaginous seeds.
Bael (Golden Apple).habitat: Dry deciduous forests and temple precincts across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal, and Odisha.
Bael (Golden Apple).active_compounds: Marmelosin, Marmelide, Aegeline, Imperatorin, Psoralen, Tannins, Mucilage
Bael (Golden Apple).watering: Low; exceptionally drought-hardy once root system takes hold
Bael (Golden Apple).soil: Tolerates poor, sandy, rocky, clayey, and alkaline soils (pH 5.0 - 8.5)
Bael (Golden Apple).toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe fruit pulp
Bael (Golden Apple).uses: Refreshing chilled Bael Sharbat during peak summer, fruit murabba, trifoliate leaves offered to Lord Shiva, and woody shells for crafts.
Bael (Golden Apple).ayurvedic_uses: Unripe fruit is the gold standard Ayurvedic remedy for chronic irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), amoebiasis, and ulcerative colitis (Grahanihara).

Wood Apple (Elephant Apple).description: A slow-growing thorny tree bearing hard, woody, round grayish-white fruits containing a brown, resinous, aromatic, astringent-sour pulp with white seeds.
Wood Apple (Elephant Apple).habitat: Dry plains and forests of Central and Southern India, including Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
Wood Apple (Elephant Apple).active_compounds: Limonic acid, Marmesin, Umbelliferone, Tannins, Dietary pectin, Citric acid
Wood Apple (Elephant Apple).watering: Very Low; thrives in dry, semi-arid conditions
Wood Apple (Elephant Apple).soil: Dry, rocky, poor, and moderately saline soils
Wood Apple (Elephant Apple).toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; hard shell prevents accidental ingestion
Wood Apple (Elephant Apple).uses: Zesty Kaitha chutney with green chilies and jaggery, sour fruit drinks, wood apple jam, and crushed pulp for digestive treats.
Wood Apple (Elephant Apple).ayurvedic_uses: Kapittha is Grahi (astringent bowel binder); cures diarrhea, throat hoarseness, hiccough, and cleanses oral toxins.

Indian Jujube (Ber).description: A spiny, drought-proof small tree yielding round or oval fruits that turn yellow to mahogany red with crisp, sweet-tart white flesh and a central stone.
Indian Jujube (Ber).habitat: Dry, arid zones of Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Gujarat, and Maharashtra; common winter street fruit.
Indian Jujube (Ber).active_compounds: Jujuboside, Betulinic acid, Oleanolic acid, Ziziphin, Vitamin C (higher than citrus)
Indian Jujube (Ber).watering: Very Low; deep taproots survive extreme aridity and heat up to 48°C
Indian Jujube (Ber).soil: Poor sandy, gravelly, saline, or alkaline wasteland soils
Indian Jujube (Ber).toxicity_pets: Flesh non-toxic; hard stone can cause choking or gastrointestinal obstruction in dogs
Indian Jujube (Ber).uses: Winter table fruit, sweet-sour pickles, dried ber snacks, lac insect culture, and thorny livestock fencing.
Indian Jujube (Ber).ayurvedic_uses: Badari soothes burning sensations; purifies blood; pacifies Vata and Pitta; eases fatigue, diarrhea, and enhances sleep quality.

Rice.description: The primary staple food grain of India, an annual cereal grass cultivated in flooded wetlands that feeds over half the country's population.
