Rice.habitat: Major agricultural floodplains of West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and Tamil Nadu.
Rice.active_compounds: Amylose, Amylopectin, Oryzanol, Tocotrienols, Thiamine (Vitamin B1), Dietary fiber in brown rice
Rice.watering: Very High; grown in standing flooded water (5-10 cm depth) throughout active tillering
Rice.soil: Heavy alluvial, clay, or clay-loam soils with impervious subsoil that prevents water percolation
Rice.toxicity_pets: Cooked rice is completely non-toxic and a veterinary standard bland diet for dogs with upset stomachs
Rice.uses: Primary staple food (steamed rice, biryani, idli, dosa), rice bran oil, flattened rice (poha), puffed rice (murmura), and straw for livestock bedding.
Rice.ayurvedic_uses: Shali rice (especially red Sastika rice) is Tridoshic, easily digestible, cooling, builds body tissues (Brimhana), and restores physical strength.

Wheat.description: The premier winter (Rabi) cereal crop of North India, producing grain-bearing awned spikes ground into whole wheat flour (atta) for daily rotis and chapatis.
Wheat.habitat: The fertile Indo-Gangetic plains of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
Wheat.active_compounds: Gluten (gliadin and glutenin), Dietary insoluble fiber, Ferulic acid, Alkylresorcinols, Lignans
Wheat.watering: Moderate; requires 4-6 timed canal or tube-well irrigations at critical growth stages (e.g. crown root initiation)
Wheat.soil: Well-drained, fertile, deep loamy or clay-loam soils with pH 6.0 - 7.5
Wheat.toxicity_pets: Cooked wheat grains are non-toxic; pets with diagnosed gluten intolerance may exhibit digestive upset
Wheat.uses: Staple flatbreads (roti, naan, paratha), bread, suji/semolina, broken wheat (dalia), pasta, and wheat straw fodder for cattle.
Wheat.ayurvedic_uses: Godhuma is heavy (Guru), sweet (Madhura), and stabilizing; pacifies Vata and Pitta; increases Kapha; builds muscle strength and heals fractures.

Sugarcane.description: A giant perennial tropical grass with stout, jointed, fibrous stalks rich in sucrose juice that powers India's vast sugar and jaggery industry.
Sugarcane.habitat: Extensive commercial belts across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Gujarat.
Sugarcane.active_compounds: Sucrose, Octacosanol, Policosanol, Flavonoids, Glycolic acid, Iron, Magnesium
Sugarcane.watering: High; requires abundant water throughout its long 10-12 month vegetative growing cycle
Sugarcane.soil: Deep, fertile, well-draining loamy or black cotton soil with pH 6.5 - 7.5
Sugarcane.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; raw stalks are tough and can cause dental damage or bowel obstruction if chewed whole by dogs
Sugarcane.uses: Production of white crystal sugar, natural unrefined jaggery (gur), fresh roadside juice with ginger and mint, molasses for ethanol fuel, and bagasse for paper.
Sugarcane.ayurvedic_uses: Ikshu rasa is deeply cooling, diuretic (Mutrala), builds body mass, soothes jaundice (Kamala), combats dysuria, and strengthens the liver.

Cotton.description: A bushy annual crop yielding protective seed pods (bolls) packed with soft, fluffy cellulose fibers that form the backbone of India's textile civilization.
Cotton.habitat: Black cotton soil (Regur) regions of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Punjab.
Cotton.active_compounds: Gossypol, Flavonoids, Cellulose (90% pure), Linoleic acid in cottonseed oil
Cotton.watering: Moderate; needs warm conditions with moderate rain during early growth and dry sunny weather during boll opening
Cotton.soil: Deep, moisture-retentive black cotton soils or fertile alluvial loam with good drainage
Cotton.toxicity_pets: Cotton bolls contain gossypol, which is toxic to non-ruminants (dogs/cats) causing heart and liver lesions if raw seeds are ingested
Cotton.uses: Textile spinning for cotton clothing, surgical cotton gauze, cottonseed cooking oil, and cottonseed oilcake for cattle feed.
Cotton.ayurvedic_uses: Karpasa root and seeds used for menstrual irregularities, uterine stimulation, and soothing earache; unrefined seed oil used for skin blemishes.

Tomato.description: A widely cultivated herbaceous plant bearing juicy, glossy red globose berries that constitute the fundamental base of Indian curries and gravies.
Tomato.habitat: Farmed round the year across Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Gujarat, and Maharashtra.
Tomato.active_compounds: Lycopene (potent antioxidant), Tomatine, Beta-carotene, Ascorbic acid, Chlorogenic acid
Tomato.watering: Moderate; even watering prevents blossom-end rot and skin cracking
Tomato.soil: Fertile, well-draining loamy soil enriched with organic manure (pH 6.0 - 6.8)
Tomato.toxicity_pets: Ripe fruit flesh is non-toxic; green unripened fruit and leaves contain solanine/tomatine toxic to dogs and cats
Tomato.uses: Essential culinary base for Indian gravies, rasam, tomato chutney, salads, sauces, and soups.
Tomato.ayurvedic_uses: Stimulates sluggish appetite (Deepana); rich in natural acids; pacifies Vata while slightly increasing Pitta if consumed excessively.

Potato.description: A starchy underground stem tuber that is the most widely consumed vegetable in India, appearing in almost every regional savory dish.
Potato.habitat: Major winter harvest across Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar, Punjab, and Gujarat.
Potato.active_compounds: Starch (amylose & amylopectin), Solanine, Chaconine, Chlorogenic acid, Potassium, Vitamin C
Potato.sunlight: Full Sun (tubers must remain underground protected from light to avoid greening)
Potato.watering: Moderate; regular hydration without water stagnation
Potato.soil: Loose, well-aerated, sandy loam or rich alluvial soil free of stones (pH 5.2 - 6.4)
Potato.toxicity_pets: Cooked potato is safe; RAW or GREEN potatoes contain toxic solanine glycoalkaloids harmful to dogs and cats
Potato.uses: Culinary cornerstone of Indian cuisine (samosa filling, aloo gobi, aloo paratha, dum aloo, french fries), and industrial starch.
Potato.ayurvedic_uses: Balances Pitta; heavy (Guru) and Vata-increasing if consumed in excess without digestive spices like cumin, ginger, and asafoetida.

Onion.description: A bulbous vegetable with concentric fleshy layers and pungent sulfur-rich aroma, indispensable as the aromatic cornerstone of Indian cooking.
Onion.habitat: Maharashtra (Nashik / Lasalgaon - Asia's largest onion market), Karnataka, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
Onion.active_compounds: Quercetin, Allicin precursors (Alliin), S-methylcysteine sulfoxide, Fructooligosaccharides, Chromium
Onion.watering: Moderate; light regular watering; stopped 2 weeks before harvesting to dry bulbs
Onion.soil: Friable, fertile sandy loam or loamy soil rich in organic matter (pH 6.5 - 7.5)
Onion.toxicity_pets: HIGHLY TOXIC TO DOGS AND CATS; all Allium species contain N-propyl disulfide which causes Heinz body hemolytic anemia
Onion.uses: Culinary base for curries, tadka, raw salads with lemon, pickled onions (sirka pyaz), and pakoras.
Onion.ayurvedic_uses: Palandu is Rajasic; balances Vata, mildly increases Pitta and Kapha; acts as an aphrodisiac (Vrishya), cardiac tonic, and raw onion prevents sunstroke.

regional_names.hindi: हरी मिर्च (Hari Mirch) / लाल मिर्च (Lal Mirch)

Chilli.description: A pungent herbaceous subshrub producing slender, fiery green or red pod fruits that provide the characteristic heat and spice of Indian gastronomy.
Chilli.habitat: Andhra Pradesh (Guntur - major chili capital), Telangana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, and West Bengal.
Chilli.active_compounds: Capsaicin, Dihydrocapsaicin, Capsanthin, Ascorbic acid, Capsorubin, Carotenoids
Chilli.watering: Moderate; sensitive to standing water which induces root rot
Chilli.soil: Well-drained light loamy, sandy, or black soils with pH 6.0 - 7.0
Chilli.toxicity_pets: Toxic to dogs and cats; capsaicin causes intense burning pain, gastrointestinal inflammation, vomiting, and diarrhea
Chilli.uses: Daily culinary tempering (tadka), green chutney, dried red chili powder, spicy pickles, and defensive pepper spray.
Chilli.ayurvedic_uses: Deepana (ignites digestive agni), stimulates sluggish circulation, burns toxins (Ama); aggravates Pitta and Rakta if used immoderately.

Turmeric.description: A rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with broad lily-like leaves and fleshy, vibrant golden-yellow aromatic underground rhizomes known as the Golden Spice.
Turmeric.habitat: Telangana (Nizamabad), Tamil Nadu (Erode - Turmeric City), Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra (Sangli), and Odisha.
Turmeric.active_compounds: Curcumin, Demethoxycurcumin, Bisdemethoxycurcumin, Turmerone, Zingiberene, Curcumenol
Turmeric.watering: Moderate to High; requires regular moisture throughout its 8-9 month rhizome development
Turmeric.soil: Loose, fertile, organic-rich sandy loam or clay loam with impeccable drainage (pH 5.5 - 7.5)
Turmeric.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; therapeutic for dogs in veterinary-prescribed small quantities for joint arthritis
Turmeric.uses: Universal spice giving golden color to Indian dishes, religious ceremonies (Haldi ceremony), sacred tilak, natural fabric dye, and cosmetics.
Turmeric.ayurvedic_uses: Supreme anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and blood purifier (Varnya); cures wounds, improves skin complexion, and prevents diabetes.

Ginger.description: A reed-like perennial herb with slender leafy stems and knobby, fibrous, aromatic, warm-spicy underground rhizomes.
Ginger.habitat: Assam, Kerala (Wayanad), Karnataka, Meghalaya, and Odisha.
Ginger.active_compounds: Gingerols, Shogaols, Zingiberene, Curcumene, Bisabolene, Paradols
Ginger.sunlight: Partial Shade (grows well in dappled sunlight under orchard canopies)
Ginger.watering: Moderate to High; requires consistent soil moisture but rots immediately in waterlogged soil
Ginger.soil: Rich, loose, well-draining humus-rich loam with pH 5.5 - 6.5
Ginger.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic in small culinary quantities; excessive raw ginger can cause mild stomach upset in dogs
Ginger.uses: Indian masala chai, ginger-garlic culinary paste, gingerbread, digestive candied ginger, and ginger beer.
Ginger.ayurvedic_uses: Universal medicine (Vishwabhesaja); fresh ginger (Adrak) stimulates digestion, while dry ginger (Shunthi) is Tridoshic, relieving cough, nausea, and arthritis.

Garlic.description: A bulbous perennial herb consisting of a composite head of multiple small cloves enclosed in papery white wrappers, famed for its pungent sulfury flavor.
Garlic.habitat: Major winter harvest across Madhya Pradesh (Mandsaur), Rajasthan (Kota), Gujarat, and Uttar Pradesh.
Garlic.active_compounds: Allicin, Alliin, Diallyl disulfide, Ajoene, S-allyl cysteine, Selenium
Garlic.watering: Moderate; withhold watering 2-3 weeks prior to harvesting for clove curing
Garlic.soil: Fertile, well-drained sandy loam or silt loam enriched with compost (pH 6.0 - 7.2)
Garlic.toxicity_pets: HIGHLY TOXIC TO DOGS AND CATS; contains toxic organosulfates that induce severe hemolytic anemia and red blood cell lysis
Garlic.uses: Core spice in Indian tadka gravies, garlic chutney, garlic pickles, medicinal raw cloves, and roasted garlic breads.
Garlic.ayurvedic_uses: Potent Vata and Kapha pacifier; rejuvenator (Rasayana); lowers serum cholesterol, prevents arterial plaques, combats joint pain, and boosts immunity.

Brinjal (Eggplant).description: An indigenous branching perennial shrub cultivated as an annual, bearing glossy, spongy-fleshed purple, green, or striped fruits of diverse shapes.
Brinjal (Eggplant).habitat: Cultivated across all Indian agro-climatic zones, notably West Bengal, Odisha, Gujarat, and Bihar.
Brinjal (Eggplant).active_compounds: Nasunin (anthocyanin antioxidant in purple skin), Chlorogenic acid, Solasonine, Dietary fiber, Potassium
Brinjal (Eggplant).watering: Moderate; regular watering during flowering and fruit setting
Brinjal (Eggplant).soil: Rich, well-draining loamy soil enriched with well-rotted farmyard manure (pH 5.5 - 6.8)
Brinjal (Eggplant).toxicity_pets: Fruit flesh safe cooked; green calyx and leaves contain solanine alkaloids toxic to pets
Brinjal (Eggplant).uses: Baingan bharta (roasted smoky eggplant mash), stuffed gutthi vankaya, sambar, begun bhaja, and vegetable curries.
Brinjal (Eggplant).ayurvedic_uses: Vartaku is light (Laghu) and pungent; pacifies Vata and Kapha; improves digestive fire; roasted brinjal eases sleep difficulties.

Okra (Lady's Finger).description: A warm-season erect annual herb bearing hibiscus-like yellow flowers with crimson centers, followed by ribbed, mucilage-rich green seed pods.
Okra (Lady's Finger).habitat: Extensively farmed during summer and rainy seasons across Gujarat, West Bengal, Bihar, and Andhra Pradesh.
Okra (Lady's Finger).active_compounds: Soluble mucilage (galacturonic acid polymers), Quercetin, Isoquercitrin, Pectin, Folate, Vitamin K
Okra (Lady's Finger).watering: Moderate; regular watering while avoiding soggy soil
Okra (Lady's Finger).soil: Well-drained sandy loam or fertile clay-loam rich in organic matter (pH 6.0 - 7.5)
Okra (Lady's Finger).toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe cooked or raw vegetable snack
Okra (Lady's Finger).uses: Kurkuri bhindi (crispy spiced okra), bhindi masala curry, sambar, pickles, and dried mucilage used to clarify sugarcane juice.
Okra (Lady's Finger).ayurvedic_uses: Mucilaginous, cooling demulcent; pacifies Vata and Pitta; soothes irritated bladder, relieves dysuria, gastritis, and balances blood glucose.

Spinach.description: A quick-growing cool-season leafy annual vegetable forming dense rosettes of tender, succulent, dark-green nutrient-dense foliage.
Spinach.habitat: Grown in winter across Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and West Bengal.
Spinach.active_compounds: Lutein, Zeaxanthin, Beta-carotene, Iron, Folate, Oxalic acid, Nitrate, Vitamin K1
Spinach.watering: Moderate; keep soil consistently moist to prevent premature bolting
Spinach.soil: Rich, moist, highly fertile loamy soil rich in organic nitrogen (pH 6.5 - 7.5)
Spinach.toxicity_pets: Safe in small cooked amounts; contains oxalates which can exacerbate kidney stones in susceptible animals
Spinach.uses: Palak paneer, dal palak, palak paratha, spinach pakoras, and fresh vegetable smoothies.
Spinach.ayurvedic_uses: Cooling and laxative (Bhedana); enriches blood (Raktavardhaka) in anemia; pacifies Pitta and Kapha when cooked with warming digestive spices.

Cauliflower.description: A popular cool-season annual vegetable with a compact, fleshy, undeveloped floral meristem curd surrounded by protective green wrapper leaves.
Cauliflower.habitat: Major winter harvest across Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Odisha, and Punjab.
Cauliflower.active_compounds: Sulforaphane, Glucosinolates, Indole-3-carbinol, Choline, Ascorbic acid
Cauliflower.watering: Moderate; consistent soil moisture essential for compact curd development
Cauliflower.soil: Deep, fertile, well-draining loamy soil with high organic matter (pH 6.0 - 7.0)
Cauliflower.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; safe in small cooked portions; can cause benign gastrointestinal gas in dogs
Cauliflower.uses: Aloo gobi curry, gobi paratha, gobhi manchurian, pakoras, mixed vegetable curries, and pickles.
Cauliflower.ayurvedic_uses: Light, drying (Rooksha); pacifies Pitta; can aggravate Vata (producing intestinal gas) unless cooked with carminatives like ajwain and hing.

Cabbage.description: A cool-season leafy biennial grown as an annual, forming a dense, rounded, tightly overlapping head of crisp pale-green leaves.
Cabbage.habitat: Extensively cultivated in West Bengal, Odisha, Gujarat, Bihar, and Assam during the winter months.
Cabbage.active_compounds: Glucoraphanin, Sinigrin, S-methylmethionine (Vitamin U), Anthocyanins, Vitamin K
Cabbage.watering: Moderate; even watering prevents splitting of mature cabbage heads
Cabbage.soil: Fertile, moisture-retentive, heavy loam or clay-loam soil rich in compost (pH 6.0 - 7.2)
Cabbage.toxicity_pets: Safe in moderation; contains thiocyanates which can cause gas or affect thyroid in very large raw quantities
Cabbage.uses: Indian spiced stir-fries (poriyal, thoran), cabbage paratha, vegetable momos, coleslaw, and mixed curries.
Cabbage.ayurvedic_uses: Cooling and purifying; aids healing of stomach peptic ulcers (via Vitamin U); pacifies Kapha and Pitta; increases Vata wind.

Bitter Gourd.description: A slender tendril-climbing annual vine producing warty, ridged green fruits celebrated for their distinctively bitter medicinal flavor.
Bitter Gourd.habitat: Grown across the Indian plains and hills in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh.
Bitter Gourd.active_compounds: Charantin, Polypeptide-p (plant insulin), Momordicin, Vicine, Cucurbitacin
Bitter Gourd.soil: Rich, well-draining sandy loam or alluvial soil (pH 6.0 - 7.0)
Bitter Gourd.toxicity_pets: Seeds and outer rind contain cucurbitacins that can induce vomiting and diarrhea in domestic pets
Bitter Gourd.uses: Stuffed bharwan karela, crispy karela chips, steamed curries, bitter gourd morning wellness juice, and pickles.
Bitter Gourd.ayurvedic_uses: Premier anti-diabetic botanical (Pramehaghna); deep blood purifier (Raktasodhaka); Tikta Rasa pacifies Pitta and Kapha, improving pancreatic insulin production.

Bottle Gourd.description: A vigorous climbing annual vine with white night-opening flowers and smooth, light-green elongated cylindrical fruits with mild, watery white flesh.
Bottle Gourd.habitat: Grown nationwide across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh.
Bottle Gourd.active_compounds: Dietary fiber, Choline, Vitamin C, Zinc, Potassium, Cucurbitacin (in bitter specimens only)
Bottle Gourd.watering: Moderate to High; requires regular watering during vine development and fruit swelling
Bottle Gourd.soil: Fertile, sandy loam rich in organic matter with excellent drainage (pH 6.5 - 7.5)
Bottle Gourd.toxicity_pets: Standard sweet fruit is non-toxic; RARE BITTER BOTTLE GOURDS contain toxic cucurbitacins and must never be consumed by humans or pets
Bottle Gourd.uses: Lauki chana dal curry, lauki ka halwa, kofta curry, raita, and dried hollow woody shells used for sitar and tanpura soundboards.
Bottle Gourd.ayurvedic_uses: Hridya (cardiac tonic), sheetala (cooling), and deeply hydrating; calms nervous agitation, purifies urine, and reduces hypertension.

Pumpkin.description: A robust sprawling annual vine bearing large, ribbed, golden-orange flesh fruits packed with nutritious flat white seeds.
Pumpkin.habitat: Widely cultivated across West Bengal, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala.
Pumpkin.active_compounds: Beta-carotene (precursor to Vitamin A), Lutein, Cucurbitacin, Zinc in seeds, Dietary fiber
Pumpkin.watering: Moderate; water at the root base without wetting foliage to avoid powdery mildew
Pumpkin.soil: Warm, fertile, well-draining sandy loam or garden compost (pH 6.0 - 7.0)
Pumpkin.toxicity_pets: Cooked pumpkin pulp is completely non-toxic and a famous veterinarian remedy for canine constipation and diarrhea
Pumpkin.uses: Khatta-meetha kaddu curry, pumpkin sambar, erissery in Kerala sadhya, roasted pumpkin seeds, and sweet halwa.
Pumpkin.ayurvedic_uses: Cooling and nourishing; pacifies Pitta and Vata; strengthens nervous system, clears mental fatigue, and seeds act as a natural deworming agent.

Corn.description: A tall, robust annual cereal grass with broad lanceolate leaves and large cobs bearing rows of plump, starchy golden kernels wrapped in fibrous husks.
Corn.habitat: Major Kharif crop across Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Rajasthan, and Andhra Pradesh.
Corn.active_compounds: Zeaxanthin, Lutein, Ferulic acid, Amylose, Amylopectin, Dietary fiber, Anthocyanins
Corn.watering: Moderate; critical watering required at silking and grain-filling stages
Corn.soil: Deep, fertile, well-drained loamy or alluvial soil with pH 6.0 - 7.5
Corn.toxicity_pets: Plain corn kernels are non-toxic; CORN COBS ARE A SEVERE HAZARD causing surgical bowel obstructions in dogs
Corn.uses: Charcoal-roasted spiced roadside bhutta with lemon and black salt, Makki ki Roti with Sarson ka Saag, sweet corn, poultry feed, and cornstarch.
Corn.ayurvedic_uses: Pitta-Kapha pacifying; drying and light; corn silk (Maydis stigmata) tea is an exceptional diuretic for kidney stones and cystitis.

Tea Plant.description: An evergreen montane shrub cultivated as manicured hillside bushes, whose tender two-leaves-and-a-bud are harvested to brew the world's favorite hot beverage.
Tea Plant.habitat: World-renowned tea estates in Assam (Brahmaputra Valley), West Bengal (Darjeeling - Champagne of Teas), and Tamil Nadu / Kerala (Nilgiris, Munnar).
Tea Plant.active_compounds: Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), Caffeine, L-theanine, Theaflavins, Thearubigins, Catechins
Tea Plant.sunlight: Partial Shade to Full Sun with high mist and mountain humidity
Tea Plant.watering: High; requires abundant rainfall (150-250 cm annually) with steep hillside runoff to prevent standing water
Tea Plant.soil: Deep, well-drained, acidic mountain soils rich in organic matter (pH 4.5 - 5.5)
Tea Plant.toxicity_pets: Toxic to dogs and cats; caffeine content causes tachycardia, hypertension, and tremors if brewed tea or dry leaves are eaten
Tea Plant.uses: Indian masala chai with milk and spices, premium orthodox Darjeeling single-estate tea, green tea, and skincare antioxidant extracts.
Tea Plant.ayurvedic_uses: Stimulates mental alertness and digestive fire (Deepana); relieves fatigue and lethargy; balances Kapha while aggravating Pitta in excess.

Coffee Plant.description: An evergreen shade-grown shrub featuring glossy dark leaves, fragrant white blossoms, and crimson 'cherries' enclosing two coffee beans.
Coffee Plant.habitat: Shaded forest canopy plantations across Karnataka (Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu - birthplace of Indian coffee), Kerala (Wayanad), and Tamil Nadu.
Coffee Plant.active_compounds: Caffeine, Chlorogenic acid, Caffeic acid, Trigonelline, Cafestol, Kahweol
Coffee Plant.sunlight: Partial Shade (grown traditionally under two-tier forest shade canopy)
Coffee Plant.watering: Moderate to High; requires seasonal 'blossom showers' followed by dry ripening weather
Coffee Plant.soil: Deep, porous, fertile forest humus and rich volcanic/lateritic loam (pH 6.0 - 6.5)
Coffee Plant.toxicity_pets: HIGHLY TOXIC TO DOGS AND CATS; caffeine stimulates central nervous and cardiovascular collapse
Coffee Plant.uses: Traditional South Indian Filter Coffee (with chicory), espresso beans, Monsooned Malabar specialty export coffee, and coffee scrubs.
Coffee Plant.ayurvedic_uses: Stimulant to Prana Vayu; temporarily dispels drowsiness, opens bronchial airways, but increases Pitta and Vata when used excessively.
Coffee Plant.conservation_status: Endangered (wild populations in Ethiopia; widely cultivated in India)

Pepper (Black Pepper).description: The King of Spices, a perennial woody climbing vine indigenous to the Malabar coast, bearing spikes of drupe berries that dry into wrinkled black peppercorns.
Pepper (Black Pepper).habitat: Tropical rainforests of the Western Ghats across Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
Pepper (Black Pepper).active_compounds: Piperine (bio-enhancer), Chavicine, Piperidine, Caryophyllene, Pinene, Limonene
Pepper (Black Pepper).sunlight: Dappled sunlight / Partial Shade (climbs support trees like silver oak or areca nut palms)
Pepper (Black Pepper).watering: High; requires abundant monsoonal rains and high humidity
Pepper (Black Pepper).soil: Heavy organic, well-drained red laterite or fertile forest loams (pH 5.5 - 6.5)
Pepper (Black Pepper).toxicity_pets: Toxic in significant quantities; piperine severely irritates pet respiratory and gastrointestinal lining
Pepper (Black Pepper).uses: Universal culinary spice, pepper rasam, garam masala component, table seasoning, food preservative, and bioavailability enhancer for curcumin.
Pepper (Black Pepper).ayurvedic_uses: Trikatu component (supreme metabolic enhancer); burns deep Ama (toxins), clears respiratory sinus mucus, stimulates digestion, and cures asthma.

Cardamom.species: True Cardamom (Green Cardamom / Queen of Spices)
Cardamom.description: The Queen of Spices, a clumping herbaceous perennial with reed-like leafy stems producing underground panicles of pale green, aromatic seed pods.
Cardamom.habitat: The mist-shrouded Cardamom Hills of the Western Ghats in Kerala (Idukki), Karnataka (Coorg), and Tamil Nadu.
Cardamom.active_compounds: 1,8-Cineole, Terpinyl acetate, Linalool, Linalyl acetate, Limonene, Sabinene
Cardamom.watering: High; requires well-distributed annual rainfall of 150-300 cm and perpetual mist
Cardamom.soil: Deep, moist, well-aerated forest loam rich in organic leaf humus (pH 5.5 - 6.5)
Cardamom.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic in tiny culinary traces; essential oils can upset pet stomachs
Cardamom.uses: Flavoring Indian sweets (kheer, barfi, laddoo), biryani, masala chai, mouth-freshener (mukhwas), and perfumery.
Cardamom.ayurvedic_uses: Tridoshic digestive; cures bad breath, nausea, acid reflux, clears throat congestion, and calms Vata nervous agitation.

Clove.description: An evergreen pyramidal tree producing fragrant crimson flower buds that are harvested before opening and sun-dried into aromatic nail-shaped spices.
Clove.habitat: Cultivated in the cool, moist, maritime tropical hill tracts of Tamil Nadu (Kanyakumari, Nilgiris) and Kerala (Kottayam).
Clove.active_compounds: Eugenol (up to 85%), Eugenyl acetate, Beta-caryophyllene, Gallotannins, Vanillin
Clove.watering: High; requires high atmospheric humidity and abundant rainfall
Clove.soil: Rich, deep red loamy or laterite soil with high humus content and good drainage
Clove.toxicity_pets: TOXIC TO CATS AND DOGS; concentrated clove oil/eugenol causes feline and canine liver damage and central nervous depression
Clove.uses: Garam masala, biryani seasoning, clove oil dental pain relief, oral mouthwashes, and aromatic pomanders.
Clove.ayurvedic_uses: Deepana, Pachana, and Shoolaprashamana (premier painkiller); instant relief for dental toothache, throat tickle, cough, and indigestion.

Cinnamon.description: A bushy evergreen tree cultivated for its sweet, delicate, paper-thin inner bark that rolls into fragrant golden-brown quills upon drying.
Cinnamon.habitat: Grown along the coastal and foothill regions of Kerala (Kannur, Malabar), Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
Cinnamon.active_compounds: Cinnamaldehyde (up to 75%), Eugenol, Cinnamyl acetate, Linalool, Polyphenols (proanthocyanidins)
Cinnamon.soil: Deep sandy loam or lateritic soil with high organic matter and good drainage
Cinnamon.toxicity_pets: True Ceylon cinnamon is low in coumarin and generally safe in tiny traces; large doses or essential oil causes mouth sores and vomiting
Cinnamon.uses: Culinary sweet and savory spice, biryani flavoring, masala chai, bakery desserts, and natural antimicrobial mouthwashes.
Cinnamon.ayurvedic_uses: Tvak is warming (Ushna); pacifies Vata and Kapha; stimulates blood circulation, balances insulin and blood sugar, and clears bronchial cough.

Mustard.description: An annual winter oilseed crop filling North Indian fields with golden yellow blossoms and producing pungent brown seeds that yield pungent mustard oil.
Mustard.habitat: Extensive winter Rabi cultivation across Rajasthan (leading producer), Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, and Punjab.
Mustard.active_compounds: Sinigrin (releases allyl isothiocyanate), Erucic acid, Glucosinolates, Omega-3 fatty acids (alpha-linolenic acid)
Mustard.watering: Low to Moderate; thrives in cool, dry winter weather with 2-3 light irrigations
Mustard.soil: Light to heavy loamy, alluvial soil with good drainage (pH 6.0 - 7.5)
Mustard.toxicity_pets: Toxic to dogs and cats in significant quantities; allyl isothiocyanates cause intense oral inflammation, gastroenteritis, and vomiting
Mustard.uses: Pungent cold-pressed Kachi Ghani mustard cooking oil, tender green leaves for Sarson ka Saag, and whole seeds for South/North Indian tempering (tadka).
Mustard.ayurvedic_uses: Deeply heating and penetrating (Teekshna); pacifies Kapha and Vata; mustard oil used in warming body massages for joint pain and sinus clearance.

Fenugreek.description: An annual aromatic legume producing clover-like leaves harvested as greens and slender pods containing rectangular, golden-yellow, pleasantly bitter seeds.
Fenugreek.habitat: Major winter production in Rajasthan (over 80% of India's output), Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh.
Fenugreek.active_compounds: Trigonelline, 4-hydroxyisoleucine, Diosgenin, Galactomannan soluble fiber, Sotolon
Fenugreek.watering: Low to Moderate; drought-hardy cool-season legume
Fenugreek.soil: Well-drained rich loamy or clayey soil (pH 6.0 - 7.0); fixes atmospheric nitrogen
Fenugreek.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic in tiny amounts; high doses can cause gastrointestinal distress and hypoglycemia in pets
Fenugreek.uses: Fresh green leaves in methi thepla, aloo methi, dal; dried leaves (Kasuri Methi) as gourmet seasoning; seeds in pickles and sambar powder.
Fenugreek.ayurvedic_uses: Deepana, Ruchya, and Vata-hara; regulates fasting blood glucose in diabetes, reduces cholesterol, stimulates lactation in mothers, and relieves joint stiffness.

Chickpea.species: Bengal Gram (Chickpea / Desi Chana / Kabuli Chana)
Chickpea.description: The premier pulse crop of India, a small glandular-hairy annual herb bearing inflated pods containing protein-packed brown or cream seeds.
Chickpea.habitat: Madhya Pradesh (leading state), Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and Karnataka.
Chickpea.active_compounds: Plant protein (20-25%), Resistant starch, Biochanin A, Formononetin, Dietary fiber, Folate
Chickpea.watering: Low; largely grown on conserved residual soil moisture after Kharif season
Chickpea.soil: Well-drained, deep black cotton or loamy soil (pH 6.0 - 7.5); sensitive to waterlogging
Chickpea.toxicity_pets: Cooked chickpeas are safe and protein-rich for dogs; raw chickpeas are hard and cause severe bloating and choking
Chickpea.uses: Chole bhature, chana masala, roasted chana snacks, gram flour (Besan) for pakoras, laddoos, and dhokla.
Chickpea.ayurvedic_uses: Chanaka is cooling, astringent, and dry; pacifies Pitta and Kapha; builds muscle strength; gram flour (Besan) used as an Ayurvedic face cleanser (Ubtan).

Pigeon Pea.species: Pigeon Pea (Arhar / Toor Dal / Red Gram)
Pigeon Pea.description: A deep-rooting perennial woody legume grown as an annual, producing yellow-and-red flowers and pods with yellow split peas that make daily dal.
Pigeon Pea.habitat: Major pulse tracts across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, and Gujarat.
Pigeon Pea.active_compounds: Cajanin, Genistein, Cajanol, Isoflavones, High vegetable protein (22%), Potassium
Pigeon Pea.watering: Low to Moderate; deep taproot provides exceptional drought resilience
Pigeon Pea.soil: Deep, well-drained loamy to black cotton soils; fixes extensive nitrogen
Pigeon Pea.toxicity_pets: Cooked toor dal is non-toxic in small portions; raw pulses cause gas and indigestibility
Pigeon Pea.uses: The foundation of Indian daily dal, South Indian sambar, rasam, kanda pappu, and nutritious dal-tadka.
Pigeon Pea.ayurvedic_uses: Tuvari is light, dry, and astringent-sweet; pacifies Pitta and Kapha; cleanses blood toxins, cools internal heat, and builds muscle.

Pearl Millet.description: A super-hardy, drought-tolerant climate-resilient nutri-cereal grass bearing dense, cylindrical, cattail-like spikes packed with greyish-pearl grains.
Pearl Millet.habitat: The arid desert lands of Rajasthan (accounts for over 45% of India's production), Gujarat, Haryana, and Maharashtra.
Pearl Millet.active_compounds: High Iron, Zinc, Insoluble dietary fiber, Resveratrol, Lignans, Phytic acid
Pearl Millet.watering: Very Low; thrives in semi-arid zones with less than 40 cm annual rainfall
Pearl Millet.soil: Poor sandy, gravelly, and light desert soils where no other cereal can survive
Pearl Millet.toxicity_pets: Plain cooked millet is safe and non-toxic for dogs
Pearl Millet.uses: Bajre ki Roti with jaggery and white butter, Bajra khichdi, fermented cooling summer drinks (Kambu Koozh in Tamil Nadu), and nutritious cattle forage.
Pearl Millet.ayurvedic_uses: Ushna (warming) and Ruksha (drying); ideal for cold winter months; pacifies Kapha and Vata; builds intense physical stamina and stamina.

Finger Millet.description: An annual cereal grass whose seedhead branches into 4-8 radiating curved finger-like spikes packed with tiny, dark reddish-brown calcium-loaded seeds.
Finger Millet.habitat: Cultivated extensively across Karnataka (leading producer), Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Uttarakhand hills.
Finger Millet.active_compounds: Exceptionally high Calcium (344 mg/100g - 10x higher than rice), Methionine, Polyphenols, Dietary fiber
Finger Millet.watering: Low to Moderate; highly resilient to variable monsoon patterns
Finger Millet.soil: Red lateritic, light loamy, sandy, or gravelly soils with good drainage
Finger Millet.toxicity_pets: Cooked ragi is safe, gluten-free, and healthy for dogs
Finger Millet.uses: Ragi mudde (steamed balls eaten with saaru), ragi dosa, infant weaning porridge, ragi cookies, and malted health drinks.
Finger Millet.ayurvedic_uses: Madhulika is cooling, strengthening, and Tridoshic; premier natural calcium source for bone mineralization, osteoporosis, and healthy weight management.

Tulsi (Holy Basil).description: An aromatic sacred perennial subshrub worshipped in Hindu courtyards, renowned as an adaptogen that protects against physical and emotional stress.
Tulsi (Holy Basil).habitat: Thrives in domestic courtyards, temple gardens, and cultivated across Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
Tulsi (Holy Basil).active_compounds: Eugenol, Ursolic acid, Rosmarinic acid, Caryophyllene, Apigenin, Linalool
Tulsi (Holy Basil).sunlight: Full Sun (needs 4-6 hours direct sunlight daily)
Tulsi (Holy Basil).watering: Moderate; keep soil moderately moist; allow top inch to dry between waterings
Tulsi (Holy Basil).soil: Fertile, porous, well-draining garden loam or potting mix enriched with vermicompost (pH 6.0 - 7.5)
Tulsi (Holy Basil).toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to dogs and cats; completely safe around household pets
Tulsi (Holy Basil).uses: Ayurvedic herbal teas (Tulsi green tea), morning chew leaves for immunity, cold and cough kadha, and spiritual home veneration.
Tulsi (Holy Basil).ayurvedic_uses: Supreme Prana-enhancing adaptogen; Ushna Virya; pacifies Vata and Kapha; cures bronchitis, allergic rhinitis, intermittent fevers, and strengthens Ojas.

Aloe Vera.description: A stemless succulent perennial featuring fleshy, serrated, dagger-like green leaves filled with a clear, mucilaginous, therapeutic gel.
Aloe Vera.habitat: Arid and semi-arid tracts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, and extensively grown in household pots across India.
Aloe Vera.active_compounds: Acemannan (polysaccharide), Aloin, Aloesin, Anthraquinones, Vitamins A, C, E, Bradykinase
Aloe Vera.sunlight: Bright, indirect sunlight to Full Sun
Aloe Vera.watering: Low; soak and dry method; drought-hardy succulent prone to root rot if overwatered
Aloe Vera.toxicity_pets: TOXIC TO CATS AND DOGS; saponins and bitter yellow aloin latex beneath the rind cause vomiting, diarrhea, and lethargy
Aloe Vera.uses: Soothing sunburn and dermal wounds, natural skincare moisturizers, hair conditioners, cosmetics, and digestive aloe wellness juice.
Aloe Vera.ayurvedic_uses: Cooling and rejuvenating female reproductive tonic (Rasayana); soothes Pitta disorders, heals gastric ulcers, clears acne, and regulates menstrual flow.

Ashwagandha.description: A small woody subshrub with ovate leaves, inconspicuous greenish flowers, and orange-red berries, famed for its pungent, horse-smelling medicinal taproot.
Ashwagandha.habitat: Dry and semi-arid regions of Madhya Pradesh (Neemuch - leading processing hub), Rajasthan, Punjab, and Gujarat.
Ashwagandha.active_compounds: Withanolides (withaferin A, withanolide D), Alkaloids (somniferine, anaferine), Sitoindosides
Ashwagandha.watering: Low; drought-tolerant; excessive moisture ruins root harvest quality
Ashwagandha.soil: Sandy loam or light red soil with good drainage and neutral to slightly alkaline pH (7.5 - 8.0)
Ashwagandha.toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic in fresh large quantities due to solanaceous alkaloids; purified root powder is used in regulated pet herbal supplements
Ashwagandha.uses: Global adaptogenic dietary supplement, vitality and stress-relief capsules, sleep tonics, and muscle performance powders.
Ashwagandha.ayurvedic_uses: Premier Balya (strength-giver) and Rasayana; calms Vata and Kapha; lowers cortisol stress, improves sleep, enhances testosterone and male fertility (Vrishya).

Brahmi.description: A creeping, succulent wetland perennial herb with small, oblong leaves and pale purple-white blossoms, revered for enhancing brain intellect.
Brahmi.habitat: Marshy wetlands, canal banks, and paddy field margins throughout the warm and humid plains of India.
Brahmi.active_compounds: Bacosides A & B (dammarane-type triterpenoid saponins), Bacopasaponins, Betulinic acid, Luteolin, Apigenin
Brahmi.watering: High; requires permanently boggy, waterlogged, or marshy conditions
Brahmi.soil: Rich, moisture-retentive wetland muck, clay, or marshy loam (pH 6.0 - 7.5)
Brahmi.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to household pets; safe natural neuro-supportive botanical
Brahmi.uses: Memory-enhancing herbal tonics (Brahmi Ghrita), brain supplements, Ayurvedic haircare oils, and wetland soil conservation.
Brahmi.ayurvedic_uses: Supreme Medhya Rasayana (cognitive and memory enhancer); enhances synaptic activity, alleviates ADHD, anxiety, depression, and epilepsy (Apasmara).

Mint.description: A fast-spreading aromatic perennial herb with downy serrated green leaves packed with volatile menthol that provides an invigorating icy coolness.
Mint.habitat: Farmed extensively in the Terai region of Uttar Pradesh (Barabanki, Moradabad - world center for natural menthol), Punjab, and Bihar.
Mint.active_compounds: Menthol (up to 80%), Menthone, Isomenthone, Menthyl acetate, Limonene, Rosmarinic acid
Mint.watering: Moderate to High; requires regular moisture to maintain lush tender leaf production
Mint.soil: Rich, moist, highly fertile sandy loam rich in organic matter (pH 6.5 - 7.5)
Mint.toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic in large quantities; concentrated peppermint/menthol essential oils cause gastrointestinal and liver irritation in cats and dogs
Mint.uses: Pudina chutney, jaljeera, mint raita, mojitos, commercial natural menthol crystals for cough drops, and pain-relieving balms.
Mint.ayurvedic_uses: Deepana (digestive fire), Rochaka (appetizer), and carminative; relieves flatulence, abdominal colic, nausea, and summer heatstroke.

Lemongrass.description: A tall, clumping perennial aromatic grass with sharp-edged blue-green blades and cane-like bulbous stalks emitting a crisp citrus aroma when crushed.
Lemongrass.habitat: Cultivated across Kerala, Karnataka, Assam, Maharashtra, and Uttar Pradesh.
Lemongrass.active_compounds: Citral (neral and geranial), Myrcene, Geraniol, Citronellol, Linalool, Limonene
Lemongrass.watering: Moderate; drought-resilient once root clumps establish
Lemongrass.soil: Well-drained sandy loam, gravelly, or lateritic soil (pH 5.5 - 7.5)
Lemongrass.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic in small traces; large ingestion of fresh fibrous stalks can cause upset stomachs or intestinal obstruction in dogs
Lemongrass.uses: Essential lemongrass oil distillation, herbal citrus tea, mosquito-repelling candles/sprays, Asian curries, and aromatherapy soaps.
Lemongrass.ayurvedic_uses: Rohisha is Ushna and Deepana; pacifies Kapha and Vata; clears fever (Swedana / diaphoretic), relieves catarrh, headaches, and joint stiffness.

Coriander.description: A feathery annual herb grown for both its tender, pungent leaves (cilantro) and its dried, globular, citrusy-sweet seeds (coriander spice).
Coriander.habitat: Cultivated massively in Rajasthan (Hadoti region - Kota, Baran), Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and Andhra Pradesh.
Coriander.active_compounds: Linalool (up to 70% in seed oil), Pinene, Terpinene, Quercetin, Coriandrin, Vitamin K
Coriander.watering: Moderate; keep soil evenly moist; drought triggers premature seed bolting
Coriander.soil: Fertile, loamy, well-drained garden soil rich in compost (pH 6.2 - 7.2)
Coriander.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to dogs and cats; safe culinary herb
Coriander.uses: Fresh green herb garnish on almost every Indian dish, ground seed spice in curries and rasam powders, and fresh green chutney.
Coriander.ayurvedic_uses: Dhanyaka is Tridoshic, predominantly cooling and Pitta-pacifying; crushed seeds soaked in water cure burning micturition, fever, and digestive acidity.

Curry Leaf.species: Curry Leaf Plant (Kadi Patta / Sweet Neem Leaf)

regional_names.hindi: कढ़ी पत्ता (Kadhi Patta) / मीठा नीम (Meetha Neem)

Curry Leaf.description: A small aromatic bush whose glossy, emerald-green leaflets are lightly bruised and sizzled in hot oil to release the soul of South Indian cuisine.
Curry Leaf.habitat: Found in domestic gardens, village courtyards, and commercial farms across Tamil Nadu (Karur, Coimbatore), Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh.
Curry Leaf.active_compounds: Mahanimbine, Girinimbine, Koenimbine, Beta-carotene, Lutein, Iron, Caryophyllene
Curry Leaf.watering: Moderate; sensitive to soggy waterlogged soil
Curry Leaf.soil: Well-drained red loam or fertile garden soil rich in organic manure
Curry Leaf.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe seasoning foliage
Curry Leaf.uses: Essential culinary seasoning for dal tadka, upma, sambar, and coconut chutney; boiled in coconut oil as a traditional dark hair tonic.
Curry Leaf.ayurvedic_uses: Deepana, Pachana, and Keshya (hair nourishment); controls chronic diarrhea, stabilizes blood sugar, and halts premature graying of hair.

Neem (Medicinal Herb).description: Intensely bitter compound leaflets packed with sulfurous and limonoid phytochemicals that have served as India's primary herbal antibiotic for millenia.
Neem (Medicinal Herb).habitat: Grown everywhere in dry plains, village common lands, and courtyards across India.
Neem (Medicinal Herb).active_compounds: Azadirachtin, Nimbin, Nimbidin, Gedunin, Quercetin, Beta-sitosterol
Neem (Medicinal Herb).soil: Grows in dry, stony, shallow, or sandy soils
Neem (Medicinal Herb).toxicity_pets: Leaves non-toxic in small amounts; concentrated neem oil should not be ingested by pets
Neem (Medicinal Herb).uses: Natural pest-repellent placed in stored rice and woolens, neem soap, acne face packs, organic insecticidal sprays, and neem leaf water baths for chickenpox.
Neem (Medicinal Herb).ayurvedic_uses: Premier Tikta (bitter) herb; supreme blood purifier (Raktashodhaka); cures skin diseases (Kushtha), eczema, psoriasis, eliminates parasites, and cures diabetic ulcers.

Giloy.description: A climbing deciduous woody succulent vine with heart-shaped leaves and corky aerial roots, named Amrita ('nectar of immortality') for its immense healing virtues.
Giloy.habitat: Tropical deciduous and scrub forests across India, often climbing host trees like Neem (Neem-Giloy is considered therapeutically supreme).
Giloy.active_compounds: Tinosporide, Cordifolioside A-E, Berberine, Jatrorrhizine, Arabinogalactan, Columbin
Giloy.watering: Low to Moderate; succulent stems retain water and survive extended drought
Giloy.soil: Adaptable to various soils, preferring well-drained sandy loam with organic compost
Giloy.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe immune-supportive botanical
Giloy.uses: Immunity booster juice, anti-viral decoctions, Giloy Satva powder, and natural febrifuge formulations.
Giloy.ayurvedic_uses: Supreme Jwarahara (fever-destroyer) and Rasayana; pacifies all three Doshas (Tridoshic); treats chronic refractory fevers, dengue, arthritis, gout, and autoimmune disorders.

Shatavari.description: A spiny, climbing woody shrub with needle-like cladodes and a dense cluster of succulent, white, tuberous fascicled roots.
Shatavari.habitat: Grows wild in tropical and subtropical dry deciduous forests and rocky hills across peninsular India and the Himalayan foothills up to 1,400 meters.
Shatavari.active_compounds: Shatavarin I-IV (steroidal saponins), Sarsasapogenin, Diosgenin, Isoflavones, Mucilage
Shatavari.watering: Low to Moderate; tuberous root clusters store ample moisture
Shatavari.soil: Rocky, gravelly, light sandy loam with good drainage (pH 6.5 - 7.5)
Shatavari.uses: Ayurvedic formulations (Shatavari Gulam), female hormonal balance supplements, fertility tonics, and lactation granules.
Shatavari.ayurvedic_uses: Premier female reproductive Rasayana; pacifies Pitta and Vata; enhances breastmilk production (Stanyajanana), balances estrogen, relieves menopause symptoms, and heals stomach ulcers.

Isabgol.description: A stemless annual winter herb with linear leaves producing cylindrical spikes of flowers that yield seeds with translucent, mucilage-rich husks.
Isabgol.habitat: Farmed almost exclusively in the semi-arid tracts of Gujarat (Mehsana, Patan) and southwestern Rajasthan.
Isabgol.active_compounds: Arabinoxylan mucilage (up to 85% soluble dietary fiber), Xylose, Galacturonic acid, Phytosterols
Isabgol.watering: Low; cool dry weather with 2-3 light waterings; rain at harvesting completely ruins seed husk mucilage
Isabgol.soil: Well-drained light sandy to sandy loam soils with moderate fertility (pH 7.2 - 7.9)
Isabgol.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; plain psyllium husk is used under veterinary supervision for canine and feline constipation; must be taken with ample water
Isabgol.uses: Bulk laxative husk (Sat Isabgol), dietary cholesterol-lowering fiber, gluten-free baking binder, and digestive health beverages.
Isabgol.ayurvedic_uses: Snigdha (unctuous) and Sheetala (cooling); mechanical laxative that lubricates the intestines, cures chronic constipation, piles, and soothes colitis.

Stevia.species: Stevia (Meethi Tulsi / Sweet Leaf / Candy Leaf)
Stevia.description: A bushy perennial herb whose emerald leaves contain steviol glycosides that are 200-300 times sweeter than sucrose with zero calories and zero glycemic index.
Stevia.habitat: Commercial cultivation in Maharashtra, Punjab, Karnataka, Gujarat, and Uttar Pradesh.
Stevia.active_compounds: Stevioside, Rebaudioside A-F, Dulcoside A, Steviol, Flavonoids, Chlorogenic acid
Stevia.watering: Moderate; shallow fibrous roots need frequent light watering without sitting in standing water
Stevia.soil: Well-drained, fertile, mildly acidic to neutral sandy loam (pH 6.5 - 7.5)
Stevia.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to dogs and cats according to the Pet Poison Helpline and ASPCA
Stevia.uses: Natural zero-calorie sweetener for diabetic tea, coffee, and desserts, herbal sweetener drops, and commercial sugar-free confectionery.
Stevia.ayurvedic_uses: Modern Ayurvedic adaptogen (Madhuraparni); provides pure sweetness without aggravating Kapha or elevating blood glucose in Madhumeha (diabetes).

Henna (Mehndi).description: A heavily branched thorny shrub or small tree bearing fragrant creamy blossoms and small lanceolate leaves that yield an iconic reddish-orange natural dye.
Henna (Mehndi).habitat: The arid and semi-arid landscape of Rajasthan (Sojat - the Henna City of the World), Gujarat, and Punjab.
Henna (Mehndi).active_compounds: Lawsone (2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone), Tannins, Gallic acid, Flavonoids, Luteolin
Henna (Mehndi).sunlight: Full Sun (requires scorching heat above 35°C to maximize lawsone dye content)
Henna (Mehndi).watering: Very Low; exceptionally drought-hardy desert shrub
Henna (Mehndi).soil: Poor, gravelly, sandy, or clay loam soils; thrives in calcareous soil
Henna (Mehndi).toxicity_pets: Leaves cause hemolytic anemia if consumed by dogs and cats due to naphthoquinone oxidant stress; keep pets away from paste
Henna (Mehndi).uses: Bridal henna body art (Mehndi ceremony), 100% natural herbal hair coloring and conditioning, and fragrant attar distillation.
Henna (Mehndi).ayurvedic_uses: Cooling Pitta-pacifying herb; leaf paste applied to palms and soles cools burning feet syndrome (Daha), reduces migraine heat, and cures fungal nail infections.

Patchouli.description: A bushy perennial herb with soft downy leaves and small pale purplish-white flowers, famous for its deep, rich, earthy-woody essential oil scent.
Patchouli.habitat: Cultivated in warm, humid coastal and sub-montane belts of Karnataka, Kerala, Assam, and coastal Maharashtra.
Patchouli.active_compounds: Patchoulol (patchouli alcohol), Pogostol, Norpatchoulenol, Caryophyllene, Seychellene
Patchouli.sunlight: Partial Shade (sensitive to scorching direct afternoon sun)
Patchouli.watering: Moderate to High; requires humid conditions and regular watering
Patchouli.soil: Rich, loose, well-draining loamy or forest soil rich in organic matter (pH 6.0 - 7.0)
Patchouli.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe aromatic herb
Patchouli.uses: Fixative in luxury perfumery, incense sticks (agarbatti), aromatherapy insect repellent, and herbal cosmetics.
Patchouli.ayurvedic_uses: Calming to the mind (Manasa Shanti); pacifies Vata and Kapha; applied for nervous stress, fungal eczema, and skin inflammation.

Kalmegh.description: An erect, slender annual herb with square stems, lanceolate leaves, and small spotted blossoms, known as the 'King of Bitters' for its extreme bitterness.
Kalmegh.habitat: Widespread across the plains and deciduous forests of West Bengal, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh.
Kalmegh.watering: Moderate; easily grown in tropical monsoon climates
Kalmegh.soil: Adaptable to sandy, loamy, and clayey soils with adequate moisture
Kalmegh.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic in small doses; intensely bitter taste deters pets naturally
Kalmegh.uses: Nilavembu Kudineer formulation for viral fevers, liver protective tonics, and pharmaceutical immune stimulants.
Kalmegh.ayurvedic_uses: Supreme Yakrit-uttejaka (hepatoprotective); cures jaundice, malaria, viral dengue fevers, purifies toxic blood, and eliminates intestinal parasites.

Shankhpushpi.description: A spreading prostrate perennial herb with hairy branches and small, delicate conch-shaped (shankha) white or light pink blossoms.
Shankhpushpi.habitat: Dry, rocky, gravelly plains and wastelands of Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, and Gujarat.
Shankhpushpi.active_compounds: Convolvine, Convolamine, Scopoletin, Beta-sitosterol, Hydroxycinnamic acid
Shankhpushpi.soil: Sandy, rocky, or gravelly arid soils with quick drainage
Shankhpushpi.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe calming herb
Shankhpushpi.uses: Ayurvedic brain tonics (Shankhpushpi syrup), memory boosters for students, and natural anti-anxiety herbal teas.
Shankhpushpi.ayurvedic_uses: Prime Medhya Rasayana (supreme memory enhancer); pacifies Pitta and Vata; cures insomnia (Anidra), anxiety, nervous breakdown, and high mental tension.

Bhringraj.description: A creeping, moisture-loving annual herb with lanceolate opposite leaves and small white daisy-like flowerheads, hailed as the King of Hair.
Bhringraj.habitat: Damp waste ground, roadsides, and margins of rice paddies and rivers throughout tropical India.
Bhringraj.watering: Moderate to High; thrives in moist and damp soils
Bhringraj.soil: Fertile, moisture-retentive loamy or alluvial soil
Bhringraj.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe herbal ingredient
Bhringraj.uses: Bhringraj hair oil, natural dark black hair dyes, liver tonics, and herbal shampoo bars.
Bhringraj.ayurvedic_uses: Kesharaja (supreme hair rejuvenator); reverses balding, stops premature graying, promotes thick hair growth, and cleanses the liver and spleen.

Gotu Kola.description: A creeping, stoloniferous wetland perennial herb with fan-shaped kidney-like leaves resembling the webbed feet of a frog (manduka).
Gotu Kola.habitat: Damp marshy lands, stream banks, and wetlands of South India, Bengal, and Assam.
Gotu Kola.active_compounds: Asiaticoside, Madecassoside, Asiatic acid, Madecassic acid, Triterpenes
Gotu Kola.watering: High; requires permanently moist or marshy conditions
Gotu Kola.soil: Wet, boggy, organic-rich sandy loam or clay (pH 6.0 - 7.5)
Gotu Kola.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe neuro-supportive botanical
Gotu Kola.uses: Vallarai memory soup, Thankuni bata chutney in Bengal, cognitive herbal supplements, and scar-reduction skin ointments.
Gotu Kola.ayurvedic_uses: Medhya Rasayana; regenerates brain cells, stimulates collagen synthesis to heal wounds, cures varicose veins, and calms Pitta fevers.

Vasaka.description: A dense evergreen perennial shrub with large lanceolate leaves and terminal spikes of white, purple-streaked two-lipped flowers.
Vasaka.habitat: Common along roadsides, wasteland borders, and foothills across the sub-Himalayan tract, Bengal, and South India.
Vasaka.active_compounds: Vasicine (quinazoline alkaloid), Vasicinone, Adhatodine, Essential oils
Vasaka.watering: Low to Moderate; very hardy and drought-tolerant
Vasaka.soil: Adaptable to stony, sandy, and clayey soils
Vasaka.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic in small doses; vasicine stimulates uterine contractions so avoid in pregnant animals
Vasaka.uses: Ayurvedic cough syrups (Vasa Asava), natural bronchodilator decoctions, and green living security fences.
Vasaka.ayurvedic_uses: Supreme respiratory remedy (Shwasahara and Kasahara); powerful bronchodilator, liquefies tenacious sputum, cures bronchitis, asthma, and stops bleeding (Raktapitta).

Sacred Indian Lotus.description: The quintessential Indian aquatic macrophyte with large peltate floating and emergent leaves demonstrating the super-hydrophobic 'Lotus Effect'.
Sacred Indian Lotus.habitat: Freshwater ponds, temple tanks, and lakes throughout India, notably Dal Lake in Kashmir and temple tanks in Tamil Nadu.
Sacred Indian Lotus.active_compounds: Nuciferine, Nelumboside, Liensinine, Roemerine, Flavonoids, Starch in rhizomes
Sacred Indian Lotus.watering: Aquatic; submerged in 30 to 120 cm of standing calm water
Sacred Indian Lotus.soil: Deep, nutrient-rich lake silt, clay, or organic aquatic muck
Sacred Indian Lotus.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe aquatic plant
Sacred Indian Lotus.uses: National emblem, edible lotus rhizome (Kamal Kakdi), popped lotus seeds (Makhana / Foxnuts), and deity offerings.
Sacred Indian Lotus.ayurvedic_uses: Cooling (Sheetala); pacifies Pitta and Rakta; stops internal hemorrhages, calms heart palpitations, and clears urinary burning.

Blue Water Lily.description: A day-blooming freshwater aquatic perennial with floating round leaves and star-like fragrant blossoms featuring violet-blue petals and golden stamens.
Blue Water Lily.habitat: Natural freshwater lakes, slow-moving rivers, marshes, and paddy ponds across West Bengal, Odisha, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
Blue Water Lily.active_compounds: Nymphayol, Sterols, Gallic acid, Ellagic acid, Flavonoids, Tannins
Blue Water Lily.watering: Aquatic; submerged roots with floating leaves in 20-80 cm water depth
Blue Water Lily.soil: Heavy clay, silt, or nutrient-dense pond mud
Blue Water Lily.uses: Sacred floral offering to Lord Shiva and Vishnu, ornamental aquatic gardening, and culinary rhizomes and seeds.
Blue Water Lily.ayurvedic_uses: Utpala is cooling and cardiac soothing (Hridya); pacifies Pitta and Rakta; relieves burning sensation, thirst, and excessive bleeding.

Water Hyacinth.description: A notorious free-floating aquatic macrophyte with bulbous swollen spongy petioles and erect spikes of lavender-blue flowers, infamous as the 'Terror of Bengal'.
Water Hyacinth.habitat: Stagnant and slow-moving water bodies, wetlands, canals, and lakes across West Bengal, Kerala backwaters, Assam, and Uttar Pradesh.
Water Hyacinth.active_compounds: High cellulose, Hemicellulose, Lignin, Potassium, Phytosterols, Phenolics
Water Hyacinth.watering: Aquatic; floats freely on water surface without requiring substrate rooting
Water Hyacinth.soil: Waterborne; extracts dissolved nitrogen, phosphorus, and heavy metals directly from water
Water Hyacinth.toxicity_pets: Contains calcium oxalate raphide crystals; chewing leaves causes oral irritation, drooling, and mild vomiting in dogs and cats
Water Hyacinth.uses: Industrial bioremediation of sewage effluents, eco-friendly woven handicrafts and basketry, organic compost, and bio-gas generation.
Water Hyacinth.ayurvedic_uses: Used folk-medicinally as an external cooling poultice for swelling and goiter; limited internal use due to heavy metal accumulation.

Sundari Tree.description: The keystone mangrove tree species that gives the Sundarbans Delta its name, bearing extensive specialized upright breathing roots called pneumatophores.
Sundari Tree.habitat: Tidal deltaic mangrove swamps of the Sundarbans in West Bengal, exposed to regular brackish tidal flooding.
Sundari Tree.active_compounds: Heritonin, Heritol, Tannins, Proanthocyanidins, Triterpenoids, Lapachol
Sundari Tree.watering: Aquatic / Tidal; thrives in intertidal brackish estuarine water with fluctuating daily tides
Sundari Tree.soil: Saline, anoxic, intertidal clay and fine deltaic silt
Sundari Tree.uses: Cyclone and tsunami storm-surge barrier, heavy water-resistant boat-building timber, hard durable house posts, and charcoal.
Sundari Tree.ayurvedic_uses: Bark and twig extracts used in tribal medicine for severe diarrhea, dysentery, diabetes, skin disorders, and hepatic inflammation.
Sundari Tree.conservation_status: Endangered (IUCN 3.1 - severely threatened by rising salinity and top-dying disease)

regional_names.telugu: కండల చెట్టు (Kandala Chettu) / ఉప్పు పొన్న (Uppu Ponna)

Red Mangrove.description: A true intertidal mangrove tree famous for its massive arching stilt roots that anchor the tree in shifting coastal mud and viviparous germinating seedlings.
Red Mangrove.habitat: Intertidal zones of the Sundarbans (West Bengal), Pichavaram (Tamil Nadu), Bhitarkanika (Odisha), and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
Red Mangrove.active_compounds: Tannins (up to 30% in bark), Mucronatone, Rhizophorin, Catechin, Lupeol
Red Mangrove.watering: Aquatic / Tidal; inundated twice daily with saline ocean tides
Red Mangrove.soil: Soft, muddy, anoxic coastal marine silt and tidal sand
Red Mangrove.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; high tannin content makes foliage unpalatable
Red Mangrove.uses: Crucial coastal protection against super-cyclones and marine erosion, marine fish nursery habitat, tannin for leather curing, and durable piling timber.
Red Mangrove.ayurvedic_uses: Bark astringent used in coastal folk traditions for diabetes, hematuria, chronic dysentery, and cleansing infected septic wounds.

Water Spinach.species: Water Spinach (Kalmi Saag / Swamp Morning Glory)

regional_names.hindi: कलमी साग (Kalmi Saag) / नारी साग (Nari Saag)

Water Spinach.description: A semi-aquatic creeping tropical vine with hollow trailing stems that root at nodes, bearing tender arrowhead-shaped leaves and pale violet flowers.
Water Spinach.habitat: Abundant in wetlands, canals, and shallow ponds across West Bengal, Assam, Bihar, Odisha, and South India.
Water Spinach.active_compounds: Beta-carotene, Lutein, Iron, Flavonoids, Ascorbic acid, Dietary fiber
Water Spinach.watering: Aquatic; grows floating on water surface or rooted in muddy saturated canal banks
Water Spinach.soil: Wet, muddy, organic aquatic silt or submerged wetland soil
Water Spinach.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; safe edible leafy green for pets in moderation
Water Spinach.uses: Popular Bengali and Assamese leafy vegetable (Kolmi shak bhaja with garlic and nigella seeds), stir-fries, and livestock forage.
Water Spinach.ayurvedic_uses: Kalamba is cooling, mild laxative, and hypnotic (Nidrajana); cures insomnia, liver biliousness, piles, and quenches summer heat.

Hydrilla.description: A fully submerged, rooted freshwater perennial aquatic plant with long slender branching stems and whorls of small serrated leaves.
Hydrilla.habitat: Freshwater lakes, rivers, canals, ponds, and fish hatcheries throughout all states of India.
Hydrilla.active_compounds: Calcium, Magnesium, Chlorophyll, Carotenoids, Lignans, Phenolics
Hydrilla.sunlight: Direct to diffused sunlight penetrating through water column
Hydrilla.soil: Grows rooted in sandy, silty, or organic bottom substrate of water bodies
Hydrilla.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to pets; safe aquatic herb
Hydrilla.uses: Classic botanical specimen for demonstrating photosynthesis in Indian high school biology, aquarium oxygenator plant, and fish refuge.
Hydrilla.ayurvedic_uses: Cooling aquatic plant applied externally in folk medicine to calm inflammatory boils, burns, and stop superficial bleeding.

Duckweed.description: A minuscule, free-floating aquatic plant consisting of tiny round fronds with a single rootlet, forming vibrant green carpets across tranquil freshwater surfaces.
Duckweed.habitat: Quiet ponds, village ditches, marshes, and canals across India.
Duckweed.active_compounds: Crude protein (up to 40% dry weight), Essential amino acids, Carotenoids, Phosphorus, Omega-3 fatty acids
Duckweed.soil: Waterborne; absorbs dissolved organic nutrients directly from water
Duckweed.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic to domestic animals; highly nutritious protein feed
Duckweed.uses: High-protein fish and poultry feed, ecological wastewater bioremediation, mosquito larva suppression, and bio-fertilizer.
Duckweed.ayurvedic_uses: Cooling and absorbent (Grahi); applied topically in classical folk medicine for hot erysipelas, eye inflammation, and chronic skin heat.
